docs.title: How to use one
docs.text:
1. In the dashboard editor, add a component, pick a data collection, then the Advanced viz type.
  2. Pick a kind. The builder ranks the kinds by how well they fit the collection (see the kind picker).
  3. Bind each role to a column under Column bindings. Required roles must be bound; the builder checks the column types.
  4. Optionally choose where the controls go under Viz controls, then add the tile.

In a dashboard YAML file, the same tile is a component_type: advanced_viz entry. A role x binds through the config key x_col:

- tag: viz-de
  component_type: advanced_viz
  workflow_tag: my_workflow
  data_collection_tag: de_results
  viz_kind: volcano
  config:
    viz_kind: volcano
    feature_id_col: gene_id
    effect_size_col: log2FoldChange
    significance_col: padj

Every entry below follows the same layout: a version badge (v1.19.0+ means available since that release), a screenshot, its input table (one row per column: the Column name as in its YAML example, the Config key that binds it, its Need (required or optional), the Type checked and an Example value), the tools whose output fits, its controls and a YAML example.

docs.title: Controls and where they go
docs.text:
Each tile splits its controls in two tiers. Primary controls change what is shown: the view switch, thresholds, colour by, a gene or sample picker. Cosmetic controls change how it is drawn: marker sizes, palettes, labels, legend. The config key controls_placement sets where they go v1.13.0+:

controls_placement Where popover (default) Behind the settings icon, or docked beside or above the plot when the tile has room v1.14.0+ header Primary controls in a strip under the title, cosmetic ones in the popover rail All controls in a column right of the plot, no popover popoverheaderrail

  • A docked panel shows the first three controls and folds the rest under More options. The component-level controls_placement (auto, right, top, popover), the builder's Viz controls section, forces the dock side or keeps the icon.
  • A reader can move the controls with the placement picker; the choice lasts the session.
  • A dashboard sets a default for every tile with advanced_viz_controls. See Tile height and control placement.
  • Every tile also offers Show underlying data: the rows behind the plot.

docs.title: Switchable views
docs.text:
Some kinds draw the same rows several ways. view is the view the tile opens on, views the views it offers. A view is only offered when its columns are bound.

Kind Views (default first) Volcano volcano, ma, qq Dot plot dotplot, enrichment PR benchmark pr, roc, both Coverage track track, locus Copy-number profile plotly, locus Sashimi plotly, genomespy

Retired kinds still load

viz_kind: ma, qq, enrichment and roc_pr_curve became views in v1.13.0. They still load and open on the matching view of volcano, dot_plot or pr_benchmark; the builder no longer offers them. ancombc_differentials loads as a DA barplot.

docs.title: The kind picker
docs.text:
The builder lists the tile's current kind first, then Recommended kinds, then the others, folded. A badge says what a suggestion rests on:

Badge Meaning Named match Columns are named for the kind's roles (log2FoldChange, padj...) Shape match Columns have the right types and shape, without matching names Fits your selection Another tile on the tab emits a selection the kind can follow, as for a Record card Weak Pickable, but a required role has no good column

docs.title: Volcano
docs.text:
v0.13.0+ viz_kind: volcano

Effect size against significance for a differential test. The same table also reads as an MA plot and a QQ plot from the view switch.

Input: one row per gene.

Column Config key Need Type Example gene_id feature_id_col required String ENSG00000141510 log2FoldChange effect_size_col required Float -1.84, 2.47 padj significance_col required Float 3.2e-08 log2_baseMean avg_log_intensity_col optional, adds the MA view Float 11.2 pvalue p_value_col optional, adds the QQ view Float 1.1e-09 gene_name label_col optional, hover label String TP53 contrast category_col optional, point colour String treated_vs_control

Compatible inputs: DESeq2, limma or edgeR results tables, as nf-core/differentialabundance publishes them.

Controls

  • Primary: View (Volcano, MA, QQ), p / padj threshold, |effect| or |log2 FC| threshold, Top-N labels, Search
  • Cosmetic: Show top-N labels; in the QQ view: identity line, 95% null band, point size

Contrasts v1.19.2+: reference, contrast_prefix and contrast_separator name the two sides (localityBarcelona reads Barcelona, _vs_ names both), effect_label can say vs {reference}, group_symbols and marker_cols set the marker shape and the Shape by control, hover_col and hover_category add hover lines.

YAML 
- tag: viz-volcano
  component_type: advanced_viz
  workflow_tag: my_workflow
  data_collection_tag: de_results
  viz_kind: volcano
  config:
    viz_kind: volcano
    feature_id_col: gene_id
    effect_size_col: log2FoldChange
    significance_col: padj
    avg_log_intensity_col: log2_baseMean
    p_value_col: pvalue
    views: [volcano, ma, qq]

docs.title: DA barplot
docs.text:
v0.13.0+ viz_kind: da_barplot

Ranked signed log fold changes per feature, one panel per contrast or one contrast at a time.

Input: one row per taxon and contrast (long format).

Column Config key Need Type Example taxon feature_id_col required String Bacteroides contrast contrast_col required String treatment_vs_control lfc lfc_col required Float 1.92, -2.35 q_val significance_col optional, significance threshold Float 0.003 label label_col optional, display label String B. fragilis

Compatible inputs: ANCOM-BC, ALDEx2 or MaAsLin2 differentials (nf-core/ampliseq).

Controls

  • Primary: Contrast tabs (All or one contrast), Top-N per panel, Significance threshold
  • Cosmetic: None

Contrasts v1.19.2+: reference, contrast_prefix, contrast_separator and group_colors name the two sides as on the Volcano and colour a bar by the group it leans toward; bars past the cutoff are hatched. effect_label, hover_col and hover_category as on the Volcano.

YAML 
- tag: viz-da-barplot
  component_type: advanced_viz
  workflow_tag: my_workflow
  data_collection_tag: ancombc_results
  viz_kind: da_barplot
  config:
    viz_kind: da_barplot
    feature_id_col: taxon
    contrast_col: contrast
    lfc_col: lfc
    significance_col: q_val
    contrast_view: all

docs.title: GSEA running score
docs.text:
v1.11.0+ viz_kind: gsea_running_score

The running enrichment score along the ranked gene list, one curve per gene set, with the set members as a rug.

Input: one row per gene set and rank.

Column Config key Need Type Example gene_set gene_set_col required String HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS rank rank_col required Numeric 1, 2 running_es running_es_col required Float 0.012 member member_col optional, the hit rug Boolean or 0/1 true, false metric metric_col optional, ranked metric panel Float 3.21

Compatible inputs: GSEA output of nf-core/differentialabundance.

Controls

  • Primary: Top-N gene sets, Layout
  • Cosmetic: Shade the leading edge, Hit rug, Ranked metric
YAML 
- tag: viz-gsea-running-score
  component_type: advanced_viz
  workflow_tag: my_workflow
  data_collection_tag: gsea_running
  viz_kind: gsea_running_score
  config:
    viz_kind: gsea_running_score
    gene_set_col: gene_set
    rank_col: rank
    running_es_col: running_es
    member_col: member
    metric_col: metric
    top_n_sets: 5

docs.title: Group compare
docs.text:
v1.13.0+ viz_kind: group_compare

Two groups of rows tested feature by feature on demand, drawn as a volcano over a ranked table. The groups come from the dashboard's selection groups or from group values.

Input: one row per cell or sample, one numeric column per feature (wide format).

Column Config key Need Type Example cell_id index_col required String AAACCTGAGAAGGCCT-1 CD3E, MS4A1, ... none, every numeric column required, each one is tested Numeric 2.31, 0.0 cluster group_col optional, groups when no selection group is picked String cluster_1

Compatible inputs: Per-cell matrices from nf-core/scrnaseq, or per-sample normalised counts from nf-core/rnaseq.

Controls

  • Primary: Group A, Group B, Test (Wilcoxon or t-test)
  • Cosmetic: log1p before testing, FDR threshold, |log2FC| threshold, Top-N labels
YAML 
- tag: viz-group-compare
  component_type: advanced_viz
  workflow_tag: my_workflow
  data_collection_tag: cell_by_gene
  viz_kind: group_compare
  config:
    viz_kind: group_compare
    index_col: cell_id
    group_col: cluster
    test: wilcoxon
    default_group_a: cluster_1
    default_group_b: cluster_2
    auto_run: true

docs.title: Embedding
docs.text:
v0.13.0+ viz_kind: embedding

Samples or cells in 2D or 3D, from precomputed coordinates or a PCA, UMAP, t-SNE or PCoA computed live on the server.

The same kind on a sample PCA, with Point size at 25:

Input: one row per cell or sample.

Column Config key Need Type Example cell_id sample_id_col required String AAACCTGAGAAGGCCT-1 umap_1 dim_1_col required Float 4.12 umap_2 dim_2_col required Float -1.37 cluster cluster_col optional String T cells umap_3 dim_3_col optional, adds the 3D view Float 0.58 CD3E color_col optional, colour by metadata or expression Numeric or String 2.31

With compute_method set, the coordinates are computed from the numeric columns instead.

Compatible inputs: scanpy or Seurat coordinates (nf-core/scrnaseq), or any sample by feature matrix with compute_method set.

Controls

  • Primary: Method (live mode), View (2D, 3D), Colour by
  • Cosmetic: Method parameters, plot style, legend, hover columns, point size, outline, density overlay, centroids
YAML 
- tag: viz-embedding
  component_type: advanced_viz
  workflow_tag: my_workflow
  data_collection_tag: umap_coords
  viz_kind: embedding
  config:
    viz_kind: embedding
    sample_id_col: cell_id
    dim_1_col: umap_1
    dim_2_col: umap_2
    cluster_col: cluster
    selection_enabled: true

docs.title: Dot plot
docs.text:
v0.13.0+ viz_kind: dot_plot

Marker genes by cluster: size is the fraction expressing, colour the mean expression. The enrichment view draws the same marks over a gene-set table.

Input: one row per cluster and gene (long format).

Column Config key Need Type Example cluster cluster_col required String T cells, B cells gene gene_col required String CD3E, MS4A1 mean_expression mean_expression_col required Float 2.14 frac_expressing frac_expressing_col required Float 0.87

Enrichment view, one row per term:

Column Config key Need Type Example term term_col required String HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS nes nes_col required Float 2.14 padj padj_col optional Float 0.0012 gene_count gene_count_col optional Numeric 196 source source_col optional String GO_BP

Compatible inputs: scanpy aggregates per cluster (sc.get.aggregate); clusterProfiler, GSEA or g:Profiler results for the enrichment view.

Controls

  • Primary: View (Dot plot, Enrichment); dot plot: Sort genes, Sort clusters, Max genes; enrichment: Source, Top-N pathways, padj threshold, Colour by, Sort terms
  • Cosmetic: Colourscale, reverse colourscale, max and min dot size, outline, labels
YAML 
- tag: viz-dot-plot
  component_type: advanced_viz
  workflow_tag: my_workflow
  data_collection_tag: marker_means
  viz_kind: dot_plot
  config:
    viz_kind: dot_plot
    cluster_col: cluster
    gene_col: gene
    mean_expression_col: mean_expression
    frac_expressing_col: frac_expressing
    views: [dotplot]

docs.title: Knee plot
docs.text:
v1.13.0+ viz_kind: knee_plot

Barcode rank against UMI count, one curve per library, with the cell-calling cutoff.

Input: one row per library and barcode rank.

Column Config key Need Type Example sample sample_col required String pbmc_1k rank rank_col required Numeric 1, 1250 umi_count umi_count_col required Numeric 48213, 312 is_cell is_cell_col optional, the cell-calling cutoff Boolean or 0/1 true, false

Compatible inputs: STARsolo, alevin-fry or Cell Ranger barcode counts (nf-core/scrnaseq).

Controls

  • Primary: Log rank (x), Log UMI count (y)
  • Cosmetic: Show cell-calling cutoff
YAML 
- tag: viz-knee-plot
  component_type: advanced_viz
  workflow_tag: my_workflow
  data_collection_tag: barcode_ranks
  viz_kind: knee_plot
  config:
    viz_kind: knee_plot
    sample_col: sample
    rank_col: rank
    umi_count_col: umi_count
    is_cell_col: is_cell

docs.title: Coverage track
docs.text:
v0.13.0+ viz_kind: coverage_track

Depth or signal along a chromosome, per sample or as a cohort median. The locus view redraws it as a zoomable GenomeSpy track.

Input: one row per sample and bin (or base).

Column Config key Need Type Example chrom chromosome_col required String MN908947.3 start position_col required Integer 0, 100 depth value_col required Numeric 812 end end_col optional, bins as intervals Integer 100, 200 sample sample_col optional String SAMPLE_01 amplicon category_col optional, colour by String nCoV-2019_1

Compatible inputs: mosdepth per-base or per-bin depth (nf-core/viralrecon, sarek, rnaseq), bigWig-derived bins.

Controls

  • Primary: View (Track, Locus), Sample layout, Y scale, Smoothing, Chromosomes, Samples
  • Cosmetic: Mark, Colour by, Show individual traces, gene strip
YAML 
- tag: viz-coverage-track
  component_type: advanced_viz
  workflow_tag: my_workflow
  data_collection_tag: depth_bins
  viz_kind: coverage_track
  config:
    viz_kind: coverage_track
    chromosome_col: chrom
    position_col: start
    end_col: end
    value_col: depth
    sample_col: sample
    views: [track, locus]

docs.title: Genome view
docs.text:
v1.13.0+ viz_kind: genome_view

A GenomeSpy track on a chromosome axis: scroll to zoom, drag to pan, brush or type a locus to filter the dashboard by region.

Input: one row per position, or per interval with end.

Column Config key Need Type Example chrom chr_col required String chr8 start pos_col required Integer 127735800 score score_col required Float 42.7 end end_col optional, rows as intervals Integer 127736600 peak_class category_col optional, mark colour String promoter, enhancer feature feature_col optional, hover name String peak_00412 sample sample_col optional, one lane per sample String H3K27ac_rep1

Compatible inputs: Any chr / pos / score table: peaks, depth bins, association scores.

Controls

  • Primary: Chromosome, Locus or gene
  • Cosmetic: Mark, point size, opacity, threshold rule, one lane per sample, max lanes, assembly, gene annotation lane, zoom to an incoming region
YAML 
- tag: viz-genome-view
  component_type: advanced_viz
  workflow_tag: my_workflow
  data_collection_tag: peaks
  viz_kind: genome_view
  config:
    viz_kind: genome_view
    chr_col: chrom
    pos_col: start
    end_col: end
    score_col: score
    category_col: peak_class
    mark: bar
    assembly: hg38
    default_region: "chr8:127,400,000-128,100,000"

docs.title: Copy-number profile
docs.text:
v1.13.0+ viz_kind: cnv_profile

Log2 ratio per bin with the called segments over it and the B-allele frequency underneath. The locus view draws the allele-specific layout.

Input: one row per bin or called segment, both in one table.

Column Config key Need Type Example sample sample_col required String TUMOUR_A chrom chrom_col required String chr1 start start_col required Numeric 1000000 end end_col required Numeric 1100000 log2 log2_col required Numeric 0.14, 0.06 baf baf_col optional, the BAF panel Float 0.48 segment segment_col optional, segment rows draw as segments, the rest as bins String bin, segment copy_number copy_number_col optional Numeric 2 label label_col optional, hover label String TP53

Compatible inputs: CNVkit, ASCAT or Control-FREEC bins and segments (nf-core/sarek).

Controls

  • Primary: View (Plotly, Locus), Sample, Chromosome
  • Cosmetic: log2 axis limit, bin marker size, Show BAF panel, gene lane
YAML 
- tag: viz-cnv-profile
  component_type: advanced_viz
  workflow_tag: my_workflow
  data_collection_tag: cnv_bins_segments
  viz_kind: cnv_profile
  config:
    viz_kind: cnv_profile
    sample_col: sample
    chrom_col: chrom
    start_col: start
    end_col: end
    log2_col: log2
    baf_col: baf
    segment_col: segment
    views: [plotly, locus]

docs.title: Contact map
docs.text:
v1.13.0+ viz_kind: contact_map

A binned Hi-C matrix, square or as a triangle under a genome track. Zooming re-reads the best resolution for the window.

Input: one row per pair of bins.

Column Config key Need Type Example chrom chrom1_col required String chr1 start start1_col required Numeric 0 chrom2 chrom2_col required String chr1 start2 start2_col required Numeric 100000 count count_col required Numeric 2841, 932 resolution resolution_col optional, one matrix per resolution Numeric 100000, 500000 end end1_col optional Numeric 100000 end2 end2_col optional Numeric 200000 sample sample_col optional String HeLa_rep1

Compatible inputs: cooler .mcool pixels dumped per resolution (nf-core/hic).

Controls

  • Primary: Chromosome, Display (square, triangle), Resolution
  • Cosmetic: Colour scale, log colour scale, row/column balance, separation drawn
YAML 
- tag: viz-contact-map
  component_type: advanced_viz
  workflow_tag: my_workflow
  data_collection_tag: hic_pixels
  viz_kind: contact_map
  config:
    viz_kind: contact_map
    chrom1_col: chrom
    start1_col: start
    chrom2_col: chrom2
    start2_col: start2
    count_col: count
    resolution_col: resolution
    display: triangle

docs.title: Transcript structure
docs.text:
v1.13.0+ viz_kind: transcript_structure

The isoforms of one gene, one lane per transcript, exons as blocks and coding parts taller.

Input: one row per exon or CDS block.

Column Config key Need Type Example transcript_id transcript_id_col required String ENST00000269305 gene_id gene_id_col required String ENSG00000141510 chrom chrom_col required String chr17 start start_col required Numeric 7661779 end end_col required Numeric 7662014 feature feature_col required String exon, CDS strand strand_col required String - transcript_class transcript_class_col optional, lane colour String known, novel sample sample_col optional String WT_REP1 gene_name gene_name_col optional String TP53 expression expression_col optional, bar beside each lane Numeric 12.4

Compatible inputs: StringTie or bambu GTF exon and CDS rows (nf-core/nanoseq, rnaseq).

Controls

  • Primary: Gene, Sample, Colour lanes by
  • Cosmetic: Colour scale, bar beside each lane, isoforms drawn
YAML 
- tag: viz-transcript-structure
  component_type: advanced_viz
  workflow_tag: my_workflow
  data_collection_tag: transcript_blocks
  viz_kind: transcript_structure
  config:
    viz_kind: transcript_structure
    transcript_id_col: transcript_id
    gene_id_col: gene_id
    chrom_col: chrom
    start_col: start
    end_col: end
    feature_col: feature
    strand_col: strand
    transcript_class_col: transcript_class

docs.title: Sashimi
docs.text:
v1.11.0+ viz_kind: sashimi

Splice junctions as arcs over a region, weighted by read support, with coverage and an exon model underneath.

Input: one row per junction and sample.

Column Config key Need Type Example chrom chr_col required String chr17 start start_col required Numeric 7670715 end end_col required Numeric 7673534 count count_col required Numeric 412, 23 sample sample_col optional String WT_REP1 annotation annotation_col optional String known, novel

Coverage (coverage_dc_tag, optional), one row per bin:

Column Config key Need Type Example chrom coverage_chr_col required String chr17 start coverage_position_col required Numeric 7670700 depth coverage_value_col required Numeric 388 end coverage_end_col optional Numeric 7670750 sample coverage_sample_col optional, matches the junction sample String WT_REP1

Compatible inputs: STAR SJ.out.tab junctions plus binned coverage (nf-core/rnaseq, rnafusion, nanoseq).

Controls

  • Primary: View (Plotly, GenomeSpy), Locus
  • Cosmetic: Junctions kept, zoom, read depth under the arcs, log depth axis, exon support, exon model lane, arc width and colour
YAML 
- tag: viz-sashimi
  component_type: advanced_viz
  workflow_tag: my_workflow
  data_collection_tag: junctions
  viz_kind: sashimi
  config:
    viz_kind: sashimi
    chr_col: chrom
    start_col: start
    end_col: end
    count_col: count
    sample_col: sample
    annotation_col: annotation
    coverage_dc_tag: binned_coverage
    coverage_chr_col: chrom
    coverage_position_col: start
    coverage_end_col: end
    coverage_value_col: depth
    coverage_sample_col: sample
    views: [genomespy, plotly]

docs.title: Gene arrow track
docs.text:
v1.11.0+ viz_kind: gene_arrow_track

One arrow per coding sequence along a contig, the way a gene cluster or a resistance cassette is read.

Input: one row per gene.

Column Config key Need Type Example contig contig_col required String NODE_12_length_84211 feature_id feature_id_col required String PROKKA_01234 start start_col required Numeric 1200 end end_col required Numeric 2850 strand strand_col required String +, - gene_class class_col optional, arrow colour String biosynthetic label label_col optional, text above the arrow String ermB region_start region_start_col optional, the lane window Numeric 1000 region_end region_end_col optional, the lane window Numeric 25000

Compatible inputs: antiSMASH or nf-core/funcscan BGC calls, Prokka or Bakta annotations (nf-core/mag, bacass).

Controls

  • Primary: Lanes shown, Lane order, Align lanes
  • Cosmetic: Highlight region, feature labels, arrow height
YAML 
- tag: viz-gene-arrow-track
  component_type: advanced_viz
  workflow_tag: my_workflow
  data_collection_tag: bgc_genes
  viz_kind: gene_arrow_track
  config:
    viz_kind: gene_arrow_track
    contig_col: contig
    feature_id_col: feature_id
    start_col: start
    end_col: end
    strand_col: strand
    class_col: gene_class
    label_col: label

docs.title: Manhattan
docs.text:
v0.13.0+ viz_kind: manhattan

A score along the genome, chromosomes end to end. mode: rainfall plots the distance between variants instead, so mutation clusters sink.

Input: one row per variant.

Column Config key Need Type Example chr chr_col required String chr1, chr19 pos pos_col required Integer 109274968 score score_col required, usually -log10(p) Float 12.4 feature feature_col optional String rs12740374 beta effect_col optional Float 0.21

Compatible inputs: PLINK .assoc, GWAS or QTL summary statistics, somatic VCFs (nf-core/sarek).

Controls

  • Primary: Figure (Score, Rainfall), Colour by, Chromosomes, Threshold, Highlight
  • Cosmetic: Top-N labels, marker size
YAML 
- tag: viz-manhattan
  component_type: advanced_viz
  workflow_tag: my_workflow
  data_collection_tag: gwas_hits
  viz_kind: manhattan
  config:
    viz_kind: manhattan
    chr_col: chr
    pos_col: pos
    score_col: score
    feature_col: feature
    score_threshold: 5.0
    selection_enabled: true
    selection_column: feature

docs.title: Lollipop
docs.text:
v0.13.0+ viz_kind: lollipop

Variants as stems along a gene or protein, coloured by consequence. With selection_enabled a click also picks the residue for the protein tiles.

Input: one row per variant.

Column Config key Need Type Example Hugo_Symbol feature_id_col required String TP53, KRAS Protein_position position_col required Integer 175 Variant_Classification category_col required String Missense_Mutation VAF effect_col optional Float 0.42 HGVSp_Short label_col optional, names the stem String p.R175H

Compatible inputs: Mutation Annotation Format tables (maftools, vcf2maf) or VEP / snpEff annotated VCFs (nf-core/sarek).

Controls

  • Primary: Gene, Sort genes
  • Cosmetic: Point size, stem width, scale points by |effect|, show stems, marker outline, palette, label top-N
YAML 
- tag: viz-lollipop
  component_type: advanced_viz
  workflow_tag: my_workflow
  data_collection_tag: variants
  viz_kind: lollipop
  config:
    viz_kind: lollipop
    feature_id_col: Hugo_Symbol
    position_col: Protein_position
    category_col: Variant_Classification
    effect_col: VAF
    label_col: HGVSp_Short

docs.title: Oncoplot
docs.text:
v0.13.0+ viz_kind: oncoplot

A sample by gene mutation matrix, cells coloured by mutation type, with frequency strips.

Input: one row per mutation (sample and gene).

Column Config key Need Type Example Tumor_Sample_Barcode sample_id_col required String TCGA-A1-A0SB-01 Hugo_Symbol gene_col required String TP53, PIK3CA Variant_Classification mutation_type_col required String Missense_Mutation

Compatible inputs: Mutation Annotation Format tables: Tumor_Sample_Barcode, Hugo_Symbol, Variant_Classification (nf-core/sarek).

Controls

  • Primary: Sort by mutation frequency
  • Cosmetic: None
YAML 
- tag: viz-oncoplot
  component_type: advanced_viz

  viz_kind: oncoplot
  config:
    viz_kind: oncoplot
    sample_id_col: Tumor_Sample_Barcode
    gene_col: Hugo_Symbol
    mutation_type_col: Variant_Classification

docs.title: Genome chord
docs.text:
v1.13.0+ viz_kind: genome_chord

Chromosomes on a ring, one chord per link between two loci: fusions, breakends, translocations.

Input: one row per link between two loci.

Column Config key Need Type Example chrom_a chrom_a_col required String chr9 pos_a pos_a_col required Numeric 130714000 chrom_b chrom_b_col required String chr22 pos_b pos_b_col required Numeric 23290000 support weight_col optional, link weight Numeric 54 sv_type category_col optional, colour by String BND, INV label label_col optional String BCR::ABL1 sample sample_col optional String TUMOUR_A

Compatible inputs: Manta, TIDDIT or SvABA breakends (nf-core/sarek), arriba or STAR-Fusion fusions (nf-core/rnafusion).

Controls

  • Primary: Assembly, Colour by
  • Cosmetic: Links drawn, minimum weight, intra-chromosomal links, chromosome labels
YAML 
- tag: viz-genome-chord
  component_type: advanced_viz
  workflow_tag: my_workflow
  data_collection_tag: sv_links
  viz_kind: genome_chord
  config:
    viz_kind: genome_chord
    chrom_a_col: chrom_a
    pos_a_col: pos_a
    chrom_b_col: chrom_b
    pos_b_col: pos_b
    weight_col: support
    category_col: sv_type
    assembly: hg38

docs.title: Fusion structure
docs.text:
v1.11.0+ viz_kind: fusion_structure

A fusion drawn as its two partners, with the protein domains kept or lost at the breakpoint.

Input: one row per domain of each partner.

Column Config key Need Type Example fusion_id fusion_id_col required String BCR::ABL1 partner partner_col required String BCR, ABL1 feature feature_col required String SH3 start start_col required Numeric 61 end end_col required Numeric 121 breakpoint breakpoint_col optional Numeric 426 retained retained_col optional, fraction kept, 0 to 1 Numeric 1.0, 0.4 source colour_by_col optional, domain colour String Pfam

Compatible inputs: Arriba or STAR-Fusion calls (nf-core/rnafusion).

Controls

  • Primary: Fusions (how many)
  • Cosmetic: Bar height, mark the breakpoint, name each domain, position axis
YAML 
- tag: viz-fusion-structure
  component_type: advanced_viz
  workflow_tag: my_workflow
  data_collection_tag: fusion_domains
  viz_kind: fusion_structure
  config:
    viz_kind: fusion_structure
    fusion_id_col: fusion_id
    partner_col: partner
    feature_col: feature
    start_col: start
    end_col: end
    breakpoint_col: breakpoint
    retained_col: retained

docs.title: Profile
docs.text:
v1.11.0+ viz_kind: profile

One curve per series over an ordered numeric axis, with an optional band. A TSS profile, a fragment-length ladder or a per-residue pLDDT curve.

Input: one row per series and x value (long format).

Column Config key Need Type Example sample series_col required String H3K4me3_rep1 distance x_col required Numeric -1000, 0 signal y_col required Numeric 6.41 lower lower_col optional, the band Float 5.90 upper upper_col optional, the band Float 6.92

Compatible inputs: deepTools profiles (nf-core/atacseq, chipseq), riboWaltz, crisprseq.

Controls

  • Primary: Log x, Log y, Local log-log slope panel
  • Cosmetic: Line width, band opacity, legend
YAML 
- tag: viz-profile
  component_type: advanced_viz
  workflow_tag: my_workflow
  data_collection_tag: tss_profile
  viz_kind: profile
  config:
    viz_kind: profile
    series_col: sample
    x_col: distance
    y_col: signal
    reference_x: 0
    reference_label: TSS

docs.title: Signal matrix
docs.text:
v1.11.0+ viz_kind: signal_matrix

The heatmap under a profile: one row per region, one column per offset, rows ordered by signal.

Input: one row per region and offset (long format).

Column Config key Need Type Example region_id region_id_col required String peak_00412 position position_col required Numeric -500, 0 value value_col required Numeric 8.7 group group_col optional String H3K27ac

Compatible inputs: deepTools computeMatrix output in long form (nf-core/atacseq, chipseq, cutandrun).

Controls

  • Primary: Row order, Max rows
  • Cosmetic: Colour scale, mean profile above the matrix
YAML 
- tag: viz-signal-matrix

  data_collection_tag: peak_matrix
  viz_kind: signal_matrix
  config:
    viz_kind: signal_matrix
    region_id_col: region_id
    position_col: position
    value_col: value
    group_col: group
    reference_label: Peak summit

docs.title: Damage profile
docs.text:
v1.13.0+ viz_kind: damage_profile

Ancient-DNA misincorporation by distance from the read end. C>T at 5' and G>A at 3' are highlighted.

Input: one row per sample, read end, position and substitution.

Column Config key Need Type Example sample sample_col required String Lib_01 end end_col required String 5p, 3p position position_col required Numeric 1 base_change base_change_col required String C>T, G>A frequency frequency_col required Numeric 0.231 length_bin length_bin_col optional, one lane per bin with facet_by: length_bin String 30-49

Compatible inputs: DamageProfiler or mapDamage substitution tables (nf-core/eager).

Controls

  • Primary: Ends, Highlight, One lane per read-length bin
  • Cosmetic: Max position
YAML 
- tag: viz-damage-profile
  component_type: advanced_viz
  workflow_tag: my_workflow
  data_collection_tag: misincorporation
  viz_kind: damage_profile
  config:
    viz_kind: damage_profile
    sample_col: sample
    end_col: end
    position_col: position
    base_change_col: base_change
    frequency_col: frequency

docs.title: Stacked taxonomy
docs.text:
v0.13.0+ viz_kind: stacked_taxonomy

Per-sample composition at one taxonomic rank, the tail folded into Other, with optional metadata strips.

Input: one row per sample, taxon and rank (long format).

Column Config key Need Type Example sample_id sample_id_col required String S01 taxon taxon_col required String Bacteroidota rank rank_col required String Phylum, Genus abundance abundance_col required Numeric 0.42

Compatible inputs: QIIME2 taxa-collapse tables (nf-core/ampliseq), taxprofiler or mag abundance tables.

Controls

  • Primary: Rank, Top-N taxa, Sort samples, Normalise
  • Cosmetic: Legend, log y
YAML 
- tag: viz-stacked-taxonomy
  component_type: advanced_viz
  workflow_tag: my_workflow
  data_collection_tag: taxa_long
  viz_kind: stacked_taxonomy
  config:
    viz_kind: stacked_taxonomy
    sample_id_col: sample_id
    taxon_col: taxon
    rank_col: rank
    abundance_col: abundance
    default_rank: Phylum
    top_n: 12

docs.title: Sunburst
docs.text:
v0.13.0+ viz_kind: sunburst

A taxonomy or pathway hierarchy as rings from root to leaf, each ring a shade of its lineage.

Input: one row per leaf, one column per rank (wide format), root first.

Column Config key Need Type Example Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus rank_cols required, root first String Bacteria, Bacteroides abundance abundance_col required Numeric 1520

Compatible inputs: Kraken2 .kreport pivoted to rank columns, nf-core/ampliseq or taxprofiler classifications.

Controls

  • Primary: Start from rank, Max depth, Colour by rank
  • Cosmetic: Palette, min arc (% of root), show % on arcs
YAML 
- tag: viz-sunburst
  component_type: advanced_viz
  workflow_tag: my_workflow
  data_collection_tag: taxa_wide
  viz_kind: sunburst
  config:
    viz_kind: sunburst
    rank_cols: [Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus]
    abundance_col: abundance

docs.title: Rarefaction
docs.text:
v0.13.0+ viz_kind: rarefaction

Alpha diversity against sequencing depth, one curve per sample, mean and SE over iterations.

Input: one row per sample, depth and iteration, one column per metric.

Column Config key Need Type Example sample_id sample_id_col required String S01 depth depth_col required Numeric 1000 shannon metric_col required, the metric shown first Numeric 3.82 observed_features, faith_pd metric_options optional, the metric tabs Numeric 212 iter iter_col optional Numeric 1, 2 habitat group_col optional, group by String soil, marine

Compatible inputs: QIIME2 alpha-rarefaction tables (nf-core/ampliseq).

Controls

  • Primary: Metric tabs, Group by, Top-N samples
  • Cosmetic: Error bars (±SE)
YAML 
- tag: viz-rarefaction
  component_type: advanced_viz
  workflow_tag: my_workflow
  data_collection_tag: rarefaction_long
  viz_kind: rarefaction
  config:
    viz_kind: rarefaction
    sample_id_col: sample_id
    depth_col: depth
    metric_col: shannon
    metric_options: [shannon, observed_features, faith_pd]
    iter_col: iter
    group_col: habitat

docs.title: Phylogenetic tree
docs.text:
v0.13.0+ viz_kind: phylogenetic

A Newick tree with tip metadata, five layouts, clade selection, filter and collapse. collapse_rank turns it into a summary by rank.

Summary by rank (View: Summary by rank, Collapse to: Genus, Top N: 12):

Input: two data collections, joined on the tree's tip labels, plus an optional third.

Collection DC type Config key Content Tree phylogeny, a special DC: the Newick or Nexus file is read as is, never turned into a table tree_dc_tag one tree, tips labelled ASV_0001, ASV_0002... Tip metadata table metadata_dc_tag (the tile's data_collection_tag) one row per tip, columns below Abundance, optional table abundance_dc_tag one row per tip and sample, sizes the summary by reads

The project declares the phylogeny DC with a link to its metadata table, see Phylogeny DCs and their metadata table.

Tip metadata columns:

Column Config key Need Type Example taxon taxon_col required, matches the tree's tip labels String ASV_0001 Phylum color_col optional, tip colour Numeric or String Bacteroidota Genus label_col optional, shown beside the tip label String Bacteroides Class, Order extra_color_cols optional, more Colour by choices String Bacteroidia

Abundance table columns are bound by abundance_col and abundance_sample_col.

Compatible inputs: IQ-TREE or FastTree Newick plus a tip metadata table (nf-core/bactmap, pathogensurveillance, ampliseq).

Controls

  • Primary: View (Full tree, Summary by rank), Colour by, Search tip, Layout, Ladderise; summary: Collapse to, Top N
  • Cosmetic: Label by, metadata strips, legend, support values, scale bar; toolbar: undo, redo, zoom and pan, reset, focus mode
YAML 
- tag: viz-phylogenetic
  component_type: advanced_viz
  workflow_tag: my_workflow
  data_collection_tag: tree_metadata
  viz_kind: phylogenetic
  config:
    viz_kind: phylogenetic
    tree_wf_id: 646b0f3c1e4a2d7f8e5b8ca3   # placeholder ids, rewritten
    tree_dc_id: 646b0f3c1e4a2d7f8e5b8cdb   # from tree_dc_tag at import
    tree_dc_tag: phylogenetic_tree
    metadata_dc_tag: tree_metadata
    taxon_col: taxon
    color_col: Phylum

docs.title: Allele grid
docs.text:
v1.20.0+ viz_kind: allele_grid

A sample by locus grid of diploid genotypes (HLA typing). Each cell is split into its two haplotypes and coloured by allele, one hue family per allele group, and a homozygous locus is one merged cell. With selection_enabled, a click on an allele filters the dashboard to the rows carrying it.

Input: one row per allele call (sample, locus, haplotype), melted long.

Column Config key Need Type Example sample_id sample_id_col required String SAMPLE_BAM locus locus_col required String HLA-A, HLA-B allele allele_col required String HLA-A*02:01 haplotype haplotype_col optional, 1 or 2; else table order Integer 1 hla_class category_col optional, groups the loci under a header String Class I objective value_col optional, side bar Numeric 1108.68 reads reads_col optional, side bar or cell opacity Numeric 1129

Compatible inputs: OptiType genotypes (nf-core/hlatyping), reshaped to one row per call; LILAC and arcasHLA calls as they are written.

Controls

  • Primary: Resolution, Order samples (and the Locus to order by)
  • Cosmetic: Allele labels, fade cells by read support, side bars
YAML 
- tag: viz-allele-grid
  component_type: advanced_viz
  workflow_tag: my_workflow
  data_collection_tag: hla_genotypes
  viz_kind: allele_grid
  config:
    viz_kind: allele_grid
    sample_id_col: sample_id
    locus_col: locus
    allele_col: allele
    haplotype_col: haplotype
    category_col: hla_class
    value_col: objective
    reads_col: reads
    resolution: 2
    selection_enabled: true
    selection_column: allele

docs.title: Pedigree
docs.text:
v1.20.0+ viz_kind: pedigree

A family tree from a PED-style table: generations top to bottom, couple and sibship lines, a square, circle or diamond by sex, filled when affected. With selection_enabled, a click on an individual filters the dashboard to it.

Input: one row per individual. Parents are 0, empty or null for a founder; sex is 1 / 2 / 0 or a word, status 2 / 1 / 0 or a word.

Column Config key Need Type Example individual individual_col required String or Integer F1_I1 father father_col required String or Integer 0, F1_I1 mother mother_col required String or Integer 0, F1_I2 sex sex_col required Numeric or String 1, female status status_col required, affected status Numeric or String 2, unaffected family family_col optional, one tree per value String or Integer FAM001 label label_col optional, text under each symbol String I-1, Proband deceased deceased_col optional, diagonal slash Boolean or String 1 proband proband_col optional, arrow; else the first affected child Boolean or String proband

Compatible inputs: A PED or samplesheet table with family, sample, father, mother, sex and phenotype columns, such as the one nf-core/raredisease reads.

Controls

  • Primary: Family, Families with an affected member only, Max families, Max individuals
  • Cosmetic: Labels under symbols, label text, symbol size, generation spacing, generation numerals, family names, colour affected by, legend
YAML 
- tag: viz-pedigree
  component_type: advanced_viz
  workflow_tag: my_workflow
  data_collection_tag: samples
  viz_kind: pedigree
  config:
    viz_kind: pedigree
    individual_col: individual
    father_col: father
    mother_col: mother
    sex_col: sex
    status_col: status
    family_col: family
    label_col: label
    selection_enabled: true
    selection_column: individual

docs.title: Ideogram
docs.text:
v1.20.0+ viz_kind: ideogram

A karyotype: one bar per chromosome scaled to its length, with a glyph per feature or density bins on it, one karyotype per genome or sample. Click a chromosome to open it with its own bins, a bp axis and zoom; from there the dashboard can be filtered to the chromosome or the visible range.

Input: one row per feature or window, on a chromosome.

Column Config key Need Type Example chrom chrom_col required String chr1, X start start_col required Numeric 1000000 end end_col required Numeric 2000000 value value_col optional, density on a colour scale Numeric 12.4 svtype category_col optional, categorical colour String DEL, complete sample sample_col optional, one karyotype per value String NA12878_75M label label_col optional, hover name String DEL sequence_length chrom_length_col optional, else assembly, else the last feature Numeric 248956422

Compatible inputs: Structural variants from nf-core/sarek, BUSCO placements and telomeric repeats from nf-core/genomeqc, variant density per window from a VCF.

Controls

  • Primary: Genome, Go to chromosome, Draw features as (Auto, Marks, Density)
  • Cosmetic: Assembly, Bars (rows or columns), Colour (category or value), bin size, colour scale, feature opacity
YAML 
- tag: viz-ideogram
  component_type: advanced_viz
  workflow_tag: my_workflow
  data_collection_tag: sv_calls
  viz_kind: ideogram
  config:
    viz_kind: ideogram
    chrom_col: chrom
    start_col: pos
    end_col: end
    category_col: svtype
    sample_col: sample
    label_col: svtype
    assembly: hg38
    mode: auto
    orientation: horizontal

docs.title: Spatial cells
docs.text:
v1.20.0+ viz_kind: spatial_cells

Segmented cells where they sit in the image: one marker per cell at its centroid, sized by its area, coloured by a marker picked in the panel or by cell type, optionally over an image of the sample. A lasso selects cells.

Input: one row per segmented cell, wide: one intensity column per marker.

Column Config key Need Type Example cell_key cell_id_col required, unique across samples String or Integer TEST1\|Cellpose\|1 X_centroid x_col required Numeric 395.4 Y_centroid y_col required, grows downwards Numeric 16.8 DNA_6, CD45, ... value_columns or value_columns_pattern optional, the markers to pick from Numeric 14242.9 segmenter category_col optional, categorical colour String Cellpose sample sample_col optional, one image each String TEST1 Area area_col optional, sizes the marker Numeric 180

Compatible inputs: MCQUANT cell tables.

Controls

  • Primary: Marker, Colour (marker or category), Sample, Transform (Linear, asinh, log1p)
  • Cosmetic: Clip low and high, asinh cofactor, colour scale, reverse scale, size by area, size, opacity, Y axis, Samples (one or side by side), image underlay and opacity, legend, hover columns
YAML 
- tag: viz-spatial-cells
  component_type: advanced_viz
  workflow_tag: my_workflow
  data_collection_tag: mcquant_cells
  viz_kind: spatial_cells
  config:
    viz_kind: spatial_cells
    cell_id_col: cell_key
    x_col: X_centroid
    y_col: Y_centroid
    category_col: segmenter
    sample_col: sample
    area_col: Area
    value_columns: [DNA_6, CD45, CD57]
    color_by: value
    transform: asinh
    selection_enabled: true
    selection_column: cell_key

docs.title: Scatter (X/Y)
docs.text:
v1.11.0+ viz_kind: scatter_xy

Numeric against numeric, with a size column, a reference line, log axes and a selection key.

Input: one row per point.

Column Config key Need Type Example rep_a x_col required Numeric 812.4, 15.2 rep_b y_col required Numeric 790.1, 22.8 gene label_col optional, hover and selection label String GAPDH mean_expression size_col optional, marker size Numeric 801.3 biotype color_col optional, marker colour String protein_coding

Compatible inputs: Any table with two numeric columns: replicate concordance, QC metric pairs.

Controls

  • Primary: Cloud (Points, Density), Log x, Log y, Reference line, Reference value, Highlight
  • Cosmetic: Marker size, opacity, marker outline, top-N labels, colourscale, legend
YAML 
- tag: viz-scatter-xy
  component_type: advanced_viz
  workflow_tag: my_workflow
  data_collection_tag: normalised_counts
  viz_kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    viz_kind: scatter_xy
    x_col: rep_a
    y_col: rep_b
    label_col: gene
    size_col: mean_expression
    reference_line: diagonal
    log_x: true
    log_y: true

docs.title: Hierarchical heatmap
docs.text:
v0.13.0+ viz_kind: complex_heatmap

A clustered matrix with dendrograms and annotation tracks, computed on the server.

Input: one row per sample, one numeric column per gene (wide format).

Column Config key Need Type Example sample_id index_column required String ctrl_1, treat_1 TP53, EGFR, ... value_columns required, every numeric column when unset Numeric 9.81, 7.42 condition row_annotation_cols optional, annotation strip String control, treated

Compatible inputs: A normalised count matrix such as DESeq2 vst() (nf-core/rnaseq, differentialabundance).

Controls

  • Primary: Normalisation, Clustering method, Cluster rows, Cluster columns
  • Cosmetic: Row annotations, column annotations

Height v1.19.3+: max_rows (3 to 16) lets the tile grow to fit a large matrix, up to that many grid rows; unset, it keeps its layout height and only shrinks for a small matrix. min_cell_px (2 to 40, 12 when unset) is the shortest row height the tile asks the grid for.

YAML 
- tag: viz-complex-heatmap
  component_type: advanced_viz
  workflow_tag: my_workflow
  data_collection_tag: vst_matrix
  viz_kind: complex_heatmap
  config:
    viz_kind: complex_heatmap
    index_column: sample_id
    row_annotation_cols: [condition]
    normalize: row_z
    cluster_method: ward

docs.title: Record card

v1.13.0+ viz_kind: record_card

One row of a collection as labelled fields and links, following a selection made in another tile.

Column Config key Need Type Example feature_id id_col required, matched against the selection String ENSG00000141510 gene_symbol title_col optional, card heading String TP53

docs.title: Ranked table
docs.text:
v1.20.0+ viz_kind: ranked_table

A leaderboard of candidates ordered by a score: medals on the first three, badges coloured by value and bars in the cells, the fields behind a row in a hover popover. With selection_enabled, a click on a row filters the dashboard to it.

Input: one row per candidate (a variant, a gene). Every other column is named in the config (columns, popover_columns), not bound as a role.

Column Config key Need Type Example gene title_col required, bold row name String or Integer TPTE rank_score score_col required, orders the rows Numeric 14 hgvs_p subtitle_col optional, monospace beside the title String p.Arg229Ter rank rank_col optional, shown in the medal Numeric 1

Compatible inputs: Ranked variants (nf-core/raredisease), outlier genes (nf-core/drop), somatic variants by priority (nf-core/sarek).

Controls

docs.text: Structure prediction, protein annotation and protein family runs publish a model, the alignment behind it and per-residue facts. Eight kinds draw them and stay linked by residue. docs.title: Architecture
docs.text: Depictio is built on a modern microservices architecture that provides flexibility, scalability, and maintainability.

docs.title: Microservices Overview
docs.text: Depictio's architecture consists of six main components organized by category:

docs.title: Core Services
docs.text: Component Technology Purpose Backend FastAPI RESTful API, authentication, business logic Frontend React + Vite + Mantine Vite SPA; canonical URLs in v1.0.0

docs.title: Data Layer
docs.text: Component Technology Purpose Database MongoDB Metadata, users, configurations Storage S3 (SeaweedFS when bundled) Data files, Delta Lake tables

docs.title: Infrastructure
docs.text: Component Technology Purpose Cache/Broker Redis Caching, session storage, Celery task broker Worker Celery (Optional) Background task processing

docs.title: FastAPI Backend
docs.text:
The backend service is built with FastAPI, a modern, high-performance web framework:

  • RESTful API endpoints for all platform functionality
  • JWT-based authentication and authorization
  • Asynchronous request handling for improved performance
  • Pydantic models for data validation and serialization
  • Beanie ODM for MongoDB integration

docs.title: MongoDB Database
docs.text:
MongoDB serves as the primary database, storing:

  • User accounts and authentication information
  • Project metadata and configurations
  • :material-workflow: Workflow definitions and run information
  • Dashboard layouts, structure, and content
  • Data collection metadata

docs.title: S3 Storage
docs.text:
S3-compatible object storage holds:

  • Processed data ready for visualization (Delta Lake format)
  • Genome-browser compatible data
  • Large file assets

Docker Compose and the Helm chart bundle SeaweedFS as the store since v1.12.0 (MinIO before). Any S3 endpoint can replace it: see External S3.

docs.title: Redis Cache/Broker
docs.text:
Redis serves dual purposes in Depictio:

  • Caching: DataFrame caching and session storage for improved performance
  • Task Broker: Message broker and result backend for Celery background tasks

docs.title: Frontend — React viewer
docs.text:
The frontend is a Vite + Mantine React SPA (depictio/viewer/, shared packages/depictio-react-core/), graduating onto canonical URLs in v1.0.0. It provides:

  • Interactive data visualization components
  • Real-time data updates
  • Draggable and customizable dashboard layouts
  • Integration with the backend API

The legacy Plotly Dash frontend was removed in v0.13.12. See the changelog for the full migration history.

docs.title: React SPA Surfaces (v1.0.0+)
docs.text:
The React viewer (depictio/viewer/) is a single Vite SPA served by nginx with a fallback rewrite. It exposes three logical surfaces against the same FastAPI backend:

Surface URL Pattern Purpose Management /dashboards, /projects, /admin Dashboard listing, project management, admin panel Viewer /dashboard/{id} Read-only dashboard viewing Editor /dashboard-edit/{id} Dashboard editing and component creation

During the v0.12–v0.13 series the same surfaces ran at /*-beta paths alongside the legacy Dash frontend. Dash was removed in v0.13.12; the *-beta suffix paths redirect to canonical in v1.0.0.

docs.title: Background Processing (v0.6.0+)
docs.text:
Depictio supports background task processing using Celery and Redis for computations that would otherwise block the UI.

┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐
│ React/API   │────▶│  Celery Worker  │────▶│    Redis    │
│  (Editor)   │     │                 │     │  (Broker)   │
└─────────────┘     └─────────────────┘     └─────────────┘

The FastAPI backend submits tasks to Celery workers, which use Redis as both a message broker (for task queuing) and result backend (for storing task results).

docs.title: When Background Processing is Used
docs.text: Context Background Processing Editor (design mode) Always required Viewer app Optional (DEPICTIO_CELERY_ENABLED) Management app Never (no heavy computations)

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
To enable background processing:

  1. Set the environment variable in your .env file or Docker Compose configuration:
DEPICTIO_CELERY_ENABLED=true
  1. Restart the full Docker Compose stack to apply the change:
docker compose down && docker compose up -d

Full Restart Required

After changing DEPICTIO_CELERY_ENABLED, you must restart the entire Docker Compose stack for the change to take effect across all services.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Variable Default Description DEPICTIO_CELERY_ENABLED false Enable background callbacks DEPICTIO_CELERY_BROKER_HOST redis Redis broker hostname DEPICTIO_CELERY_BROKER_PORT 6379 Redis broker port DEPICTIO_CELERY_BROKER_DB 1 Redis database for Celery broker DEPICTIO_CELERY_RESULT_BACKEND_DB 2 Redis database for Celery results

docs.title: Real-time Events (v1.1.4+)
docs.text:
Depictio can push live dashboard updates over WebSocket when the data behind a dashboard changes, so viewers refresh without polling. The subsystem is disabled by default (DEPICTIO_EVENTS_ENABLED) and opt-in per project.

┌────────────┐   upsert    ┌─────────────┐   pub/sub   ┌─────────────┐
│  Producer  │────────────▶│   FastAPI   │────────────▶│    Redis    │
│  (CLI /    │             │  event svc  │             │  (fan-out)  │
│ instrument)│             └──────┬──────┘             └──────┬──────┘
└────────────┘                    │ WebSocket                 │
                                  ▼                           │
                          ┌───────────────┐                   │
                          │  Subscribed   │◀──────────────────┘
                          │  dashboards   │
                          └───────────────┘

Moving parts:

  • Event service + connection manager (FastAPI) — track WebSocket subscriptions per dashboard and broadcast data_collection_updated events.
  • Redis pub/sub — fans events out across API workers/replicas, on a dedicated Redis DB (default 3, separate from cache and Celery).
  • MongoDB change streams (optional, requires a replica set) — detect data-collection changes at the database layer.
  • WebSocket channel /depictio/api/v1/events/ws — JWT-authenticated via a token query parameter and permission-checked at viewer level; the React viewer subscribes per dashboard and drives the live indicator.

Trigger path: a producer re-ingests or upserts a data collection (POST /deltatables/upsert) → the API re-reads the Delta, recomputes column specs and bumps the version → broadcasts to subscribed dashboards, which refetch. Activation requires both the server flag and a realtime block in the project's project.yaml.

See the Real-time events guide for setup, and the environment reference for the full DEPICTIO_EVENTS_* list.

docs.title: Data Flow
docs.text:
┌─────────┐     ┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────┐
│  CLI    │────▶│  FastAPI    │────▶│  MongoDB    │◀────│  React  │
│         │     │  Backend    │     │             │     │  Viewer │
└─────────┘     └──────┬──────┘     └─────────────┘     └────┬────┘
                       │                                      │
                       ▼                                      │
                ┌─────────────┐                               │
                │   S3        │◀──────────────────────────────┘
                │  (Delta)    │
                └─────────────┘
  1. CLI ingests data, validates, stores in Delta format, registers in MongoDB
  2. API serves metadata and data access endpoints
  3. React viewer renders interactive visualizations, calls API for data

docs.title: Comments and Annotations
docs.text: Discuss a dashboard where the data is: comment threads on a component or a whole tab, and annotations drawn on top of charts, tables and maps.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
There are two things you can attach to a dashboard:

  • Comments: a thread on one component, or on the whole tab. Threads take replies, can be resolved and reopened, and remember the filters and the selection that were active when they were written.
  • Annotations: a shape drawn on a component, in the style of newsroom charts: a highlighted range, a reference line, a set of marked points or rows, or a note with an arrow. Every annotation is also a thread, so it has the same badge, the same drawer and the same discussion as a plain comment.

One section of the Palmer Penguins dashboard with annotations on four charts: x and y ranges, reference lines, arrow notes, marked points inside a shaded box or lasso region, and rings on box-plot outliers.

Stored outside the dashboard

Threads and annotations are kept in their own MongoDB collection, not in the dashboard document. Saving the dashboard or editing its layout never drops them, and after a YAML re-import they re-attach to their components (see below). They are not part of a dashboard's YAML export, but backups include them. Deleting a dashboard, a tab or a project deletes its threads. Annotations are drawn by the viewer on top of the figure at render time: nothing is recomputed on the server, and the component's own definition is unchanged.

Comments and annotations live in the dashboard viewer (/dashboard/{id}), not in the editor.

docs.title: Who can see what
docs.text:
Who Comments and annotations Project owners and editors Read and write every thread on the project's dashboards Instance admins Same as owners Project viewers No threads, no badge, no drawer. They see only the annotations switched to Visible to viewers, as a shape and a label. With viewers can comment on, they read and write threads Visitors of a public project, anonymous users Same as viewers: published annotations only, never a discussion Single-user mode The session is the instance admin, so everything is available

The discussion itself is never shown to viewers. Publishing an annotation exposes its shape, its colour and its label, nothing else.

Thread actions follow the author:

  • an editor or owner can reply, resolve, reopen, edit an annotation and change its visibility;
  • you can edit or delete your own comments; a project owner can also delete anyone's comment (it is replaced by Comment deleted);
  • a whole thread can be deleted by its author, a project owner or an admin.

docs.title: Viewers can comment (v1.17.2+)
docs.text:
A showcase instance may want remarks from the people it shows a dashboard to, without giving them edit rights. DEPICTIO_COMMENTS_VIEWERS_CAN_COMMENT=true (default false) lets anyone with viewer access to a project read and write its threads:

  • a viewer replies, edits or deletes their own comments, and deletes their own threads;
  • resolving or reopening a thread, publishing or editing an annotation, annotate mode and agent proposals stay with editors and owners; a viewer never sees proposals or rejected threads;
  • anonymous visitors and the temporary accounts of public mode never comment. Since v1.17.3 a guest is offered to sign in instead.

Commenters see each other's email addresses. On Kubernetes, the setting is the backend.env key of the same name.

docs.title: The comments drawer
docs.text:
There are two ways in, both visible only to editors and owners (and to viewers when they may comment):

  • the Comments button in the dashboard header opens every thread of the current tab. Its badge counts open threads (or, when there are none, proposals awaiting review), and its tooltip also counts threads whose data changed;
  • the comments icon in a component's action bar opens that component's threads. A number badge counts open threads, a pulsing violet dot flags agent proposals awaiting review, and the icon turns orange when one of the component's open threads no longer matches its data or its definition (see When the data or the component changes).

Left: the Comments tab on the whole tab, with a thread flagged Data changed. Right: the Annotations tab, grouped by component, each card carrying its numbered badge.

The drawer docks on the right without covering the dashboard, so clicking a thread can scroll the page to its component:

  • Scope line. Under the title, either Whole tab · N components with threads, or On followed by the component's name. The pill's x goes back to the whole tab. In the whole-tab view, threads are grouped by component; clicking a group header narrows the drawer to that component.
  • Comments / Annotations. Two tabs, each with its count. Plain comments and annotations are listed apart.
  • Show. Status chips: Open, Resolved and Proposed. Open and Proposed are on by default.

docs.title: Writing a comment
docs.text:
The composer sits at the bottom of the Comments tab. It says what you are commenting on (Commenting on the whole tab, or a component's name), and lists what will be attached:

  • the active filters (N active filters will be attached);
  • the current selection on that component, when there is one (points, bars or rows selected on the dashboard).

Type the comment and press Post (or Ctrl+Enter). A comment holds up to 4,000 characters.

docs.title: Working with a thread
docs.text:
Each thread card shows its author, the time it was written, its status, and badges for what it captured (a selection, N filters) and for staleness. Below the discussion:

Action Effect Reply Adds a comment to the thread (up to 500 per thread) Resolve / Reopen Moves the thread between Open and Resolved Show on dashboard Scrolls to the component, highlights it, and re-applies the thread's filters and selection Delete thread Deletes the thread and all its replies, after a confirmation

Show on dashboard restores the view, not the past

The filters and selection come back, but they are applied to today's data and to the component as it is now. If either changed since the thread was written, the thread says so (see below). If the component was removed, a notice says so instead of scrolling.

docs.title: Annotation shapes
docs.text:
Tool Kind What it draws Range on x / Range on y Range highlight A band across one axis, behind the data. Drag a box: only its x (or y) extent is kept Vertical line / Horizontal line Reference line A dashed line at one x or y value, in front of the data. Click to place it Mark points (lasso) / Mark points (box) Marked points Rings around the selected points or bars, optionally with the selected area shaded behind them Note Note A numbered label with an arrow pointing at a data point. Click a point to attach it

Shapes are stored in data coordinates, so they keep their place when the figure is resized, zoomed or redrawn. Marked points are stored by the component's selection column when it has one, so they follow their rows across re-sorting and re-ingestion; charts without one (bars, histograms) store plain coordinates.

docs.title: Drawing an annotation
docs.text:
1. Hover the component and click Annotate () in its action bar. A tool palette appears in the top-left corner of the figure, with a one-line hint under it.
  2. Pick a tool. Zoom and pan stay available from the Plotly modebar; while they are active no tool is highlighted, and clicking a tool again goes back to drawing.
  3. Draw. The shape appears as a dashed preview with a live count, for example 18 points in range or 40 points.
  4. Fill in the popover: a Label (required, up to 120 characters), a Color, for marked points Highlight the selected area and its Area opacity, an optional Comment to start the discussion, and Visible to viewers. Press Save.
  5. Click (or press Esc) to leave annotate mode.

Drawing never touches the dashboard: annotate mode detaches the component's cross-filtering, so a lasso drawn for an annotation does not filter or clear anything.

Annotate mode on a scatter plot: the tool palette with Mark points (lasso) active, the lassoed points previewed on the chart, and the form for the new annotation.

Each annotation gets a number on its tab, shown as a badge (①, ②, ...) in the annotation's colour, on the chart and on its card in the drawer. Hovering a label on the chart shows what it covers, such as the range and the number of points inside it.

ScatterLasso regionBox plotHistogram

A y range, an arrow note, points marked inside a shaded box, and a threshold line.

A lasso region around one group of points, with a note and a reference line.

Rings on box-plot outliers, drawn where the points actually sit.

Two x ranges on an overlaid histogram.

docs.title: Editing an annotation
docs.text:
Click an annotation's label (or one of its rings) on the chart. A popover opens in place, titled after its kind, with:

  • Label and Color;
  • for a range highlight: Opacity;
  • for a reference line: Line style (Solid, Dashed, Dotted) and Line width;
  • for marked points: Ring width, and Highlight the selected area with its Area opacity when the points were drawn with a region.

Changes are previewed live on the chart; Cancel puts the saved version back. The popover also offers Open discussion, which jumps to the thread in the drawer, and Delete annotation. The same editor opens from Edit annotation on the thread's card in the drawer.

Clicking the label of a range highlight: its hover summary, and the inline editor with the label, the colour and the opacity.

docs.title: Showing an annotation to viewers
docs.text: Visible to viewers is off by default: a new annotation is internal to the project's editors and owners. Switch it on, in the creation form or on the thread's card, and viewers of the dashboard see the shape and its label. They never see the discussion, and clicking a published annotation opens nothing for them. An agent's annotation cannot be published until a person accepts it.

docs.title: Where you can annotate
docs.text:
The Annotate action only appears on components that can take a shape. Comments work on every component, and on the tab itself.

Component Annotations Figures Every cartesian Plotly figure: all four shapes. 3D, polar, pie and hierarchical charts (sunburst, treemap, icicle) and parallel coordinates are comment-only Advanced visualizations The single-panel cartesian kinds: volcano, MA, QQ, Manhattan, embedding (2D only), scatter, DA barplot, ANCOM-BC differentials, stacked taxonomy, rarefaction, enrichment, dot plot, lollipop (one gene shown), PR benchmark, ROC / PR curve, confusion matrix, metric CI bars, profile, GSEA running score (single panel) and coverage track (single panel, not in the Locus view) MultiQC figures Line and bar graphs and other plots drawn on one pair of axes. Marked points are stored as sample names, so marking a line graph rings whole sample lines. Multi-panel figures are comment-only MultiQC General Stats Row annotations in the table view, keyed on the sample name (not in the violin view) Tables Tables with a row-id column (row_selection_column or selection_column): rows can be marked Maps Scatter and choropleth maps: Mark points (lasso or box, with an optional shaded longitude / latitude region) and Note. Ranges and lines have no meaning on a map. Density maps are comment-only

Multi-panel and non-cartesian advanced visualizations (complex heatmap, oncoplot, signal matrix, sashimi, UpSet, sunburst, Sankey, phylogeny) stay comment-only: a shape needs a single pair of axes.

Advanced visualizationsMultiQC line graphMultiQC General StatsTableMap

A significance line, marked genes and notes on a volcano plot; a genome-wide line and a peak note on a Manhattan plot; a lasso cluster on a UMAP; marked loci on a QQ plot; an NES range and marked terms on an enrichment dot plot; a plateau range on rarefaction curves.

Sample lines marked as a whole, and a quality threshold line.

Annotated rows in the General Statistics table.

Marked rows, with their badges in the pinned annotation column.

A shaded longitude / latitude region, marked sites and a note on a scatter map.

docs.title: Marking table rows
docs.text: In annotate mode a table shows a single Mark rows tool in its top-right corner. Click rows to select them, then press Mark N selected rows. Marked rows get the annotation's numbered badge in a narrow column pinned to the left of the grid.

docs.title: Components with several views
docs.text: Some components show one of several plots: a MultiQC component switching dataset, between counts and percentages or to a log scale, and advanced visualizations whose tile offers several views on different axes (volcano / MA / QQ, marker dot plot / enrichment, PR / ROC). An annotation remembers the view it was drawn on and only appears on that view, so a line drawn on the volcano never lands on the MA plot's axes.

docs.title: When the data or the component changes
docs.text:
When a thread is written, Depictio records a fingerprint of the component's definition and of every data collection it reads. Each time threads are listed, both are compared with the dashboard as it is now, and the thread card shows:

Badge Meaning Data changed A data collection the component reads was processed again since the thread was written. Any new aggregation counts, even a re-ingest of identical files Component changed The component's definition was edited. Moving or resizing the tile does not count Component removed The component is no longer on the tab M of N found Some of the points or rows an annotation marked are not in the chart's current data

Open threads with changed data or a changed component also turn the component's comments icon orange, so staleness is visible on the dashboard without opening the drawer.

After a dashboard is re-imported from YAML, components may come back with new identifiers. A thread whose component seems gone re-attaches itself to the component with the same title, when exactly one component on the tab has that title.

docs.title: Agent proposals
docs.text:
Threads and annotations can also be written by an agent, through the comments API. An agent always acts on behalf of the user whose credentials it uses, and its threads are held for review:

  • an agent's thread starts as Proposed. Its annotation is drawn faded and dashed, and it appears under the Proposed chip;
  • the card shows the agent's name, Agent on behalf of the person who launched it, and the Evidence the agent attached (structured claims backing its comment);
  • Accept turns the proposal into an ordinary open thread. Reject asks for an optional reason, then hides the thread and keeps the decision;
  • a proposal cannot be resolved, and its annotation cannot be made Visible to viewers, until it is accepted. If a person edits a proposed annotation, the card says Edited by a human.

Running the same agent again updates its earlier pending (or rejected) proposals instead of duplicating them; a re-proposed rejection goes back to review. One agent run can open at most 50 threads.

Comments are data, not instructions

The text of a comment is never treated as an instruction for an agent reading the dashboard.

docs.title: Known limits
docs.text:
• A range on a categorical axis stores category positions, so it moves if the order of the categories changes.
  • Rings on box, violin and bar points are drawn as shapes: hover and click-to-edit go through the numbered label there.
  • On charts with marginal plots, y ranges and horizontal lines also span the marginal panels.
  • When the id column repeats a value, a mark resolved by id rings only the first matching row.
  • Long labels placed in data coordinates can stretch the axis range, and labels near the edge of the plot can be clipped.
  • On maps, labels are numbered (1), (2), ... rather than ①, ②.
  • There are no mentions or notifications yet.
