docs.title: Dashboard tabs
docs.text:
One dashboard: the Overview, then six child tabs in three groups, read as a funnel from the spectra to the peptides each sample presents. Each tab below carries the same icon and colour the dashboard gives it, so the page and the app read alike.

Group Tabs Data & QC MultiQC, Reproducibility Search Identification, Physico-chemical checks Immunopeptidome MHC signature, Peptides and proteins

Each child tab opens with a short intro and a strip of four cards, then at most three open sections; tables and record cards follow, collapsed. The design comes from the samplesheet: one row per raw file with its sample, its condition (GROUP_COL, Condition by default) and its search database. The persistent Sample filters (condition, sample, raw file) sit in the left panel and narrow every tab: the links carry a pick to every sample-level table by sample_id and to the Comet tables by run_id. The Sample sheet and the Reference tables (the per-sample summary) are pinned, collapsed, to the bottom of every child tab.

Overview MultiQC Reproducibility Identification Physico-chemical checks MHC signature Peptides and proteins

Immunopeptidomics, from the spectra to the peptides each sample presents.

A short hero links the run parameters. About this dashboard says how the two filter levels work, The run lists the samples and raw files, the enzyme, the FDR threshold, the peptide length bounds and the rescoring engine, and Pipeline walks the six steps from the search to the comparison of conditions, each linked to its parameters and its tab. The key figures read collections every route writes, so a route never leaves a gap in them. The findings are live values: they follow the filters.

Filters and components

Filters · the left panel starts collapsed. Key figures has its own filter bar (the condition and the sample), and so does Findings (the condition and the peptide length): each narrows its own section only.

Section What it holds Top Hero, About this dashboard, The run, Pipeline Key figures 4 headline cards: samples, PSMs, peptides, identification rate Findings Live result rows, then 4 figures: the accepted PSMs against the FDR threshold, the observed against predicted retention time, the length profile and the source proteins How to read this dashboard The tabs by group, each with its question

Data & QC · Did the search identify peptides evenly across samples?

MultiQC panels only: the sections mhcquant writes into its own report. Open: identification counts, the q-value and Comet Xcorr distributions, then precursor m/z, retention time and peptide intensity. Compare the counts across samples first, then check that a low-yield sample's scores look like the others. The total ion chromatograms, the fragment mass error and the Percolator feature weights are collapsed, for when the cause is the acquisition or the rescoring model.

Filters and components

Filters · the pinned sample filters narrow its panels.

Section What it holds Identification yield 3 MultiQC panels Peptide properties 3 MultiQC panels Acquisition and rescoring (collapsed) 3 MultiQC panels

Data & QC · Do the replicate injections of a sample quantify the same peptides?

OpenMS aligns the replicate injections of each sample and quantifies every peptide in each. The replicates per peptide, the peptide detections as a ring by replicate, the median log10 intensity and the peptides quantified in both replicates of a pair. Then the intensity scatter for every replicate pair and the UpSet of the replicate combinations: a pair off the diagonal, or a small all-replicate core, points at one injection to check. Replicate labels follow the samplesheet ID order within a sample. The membership table is collapsed.

Filters and components

Filters · Replicate pair on mhcquant_replicate_pairs and a Replicates detected range on mhcquant_replicate_detection.

Section What it holds Replicates at a glance 4 cards Replicate agreement 1 advanced visualization Replicate overlap 1 advanced visualization Replicate table (collapsed) Replicate membership per peptide

Only with --quantify

Every tile here binds a replicate collection. A run without --quantify takes --var NO_QUANTIFICATION=true: the tab is dropped, and the replicate columns of the per-sample summary stay empty.

Search · How many spectra became peptides, and at what FDR?

The spectra searched, as a funnel to the target matches and the PSMs accepted at 5% and 1% FDR; the identification rate per raw file; the PSMs that passed the pipeline's filter; the accepted precursors by modification. Then the accepted PSMs against the q-value threshold, one curve per raw file, and the score of the accepted peptides by sample. The Comet numbers come from the pin files, before MS2Rescore and Percolator, so they describe the raw search, not the final FDR. The Comet search table is collapsed.

Filters and components

Filters · Peptide score and PSMs per peptide ranges on mhcquant_peptides.

Section What it holds Yield at a glance 4 cards Search and FDR 1 advanced visualization + Score of the accepted peptides Search table (collapsed) Comet search yield per raw file

Search · Do the identified peptides elute and ionise as peptides should?

The retention-time error per sample, the precursor mass error per raw file, the correlation with the MS2PIP-predicted spectrum and the precursors by charge. Then the observed against DeepLC-predicted retention time, with the record of a picked peptide beside it, and side by side retention time against Kyte-Doolittle hydropathy and precursor m/z over the gradient by charge. Outliers on these plots are the identifications to question first. The fragment-ion cards and table are collapsed.

Filters and components

Filters · Precursor charge and a Retention time (min) range on mhcquant_peptides.

Section What it holds Accuracy at a glance 4 cards Chromatography 1 advanced visualization + a peptide record card Hydropathy and charge 2 advanced visualizations Fragment ions (collapsed) 2 cards, Matched fragment ions per peptide

Only with --annotate_ions

A run without --annotate_ions takes --var NO_ION_ANNOTATION=true, and the Fragment ions section is dropped.

Immunopeptidome · Which MHC class do the peptide lengths and anchor motifs point to?

The 9-mer share per sample, the median peptide length, and the distinct sequences ranked by their P2 and C-terminal residues, the two class I anchors. Then the length profile with the class I (8 to 12) and class II (13 to 25) ranges shaded, the composition per sample by length, switchable to charge and modification, and the amino-acid frequency at each position per sample and length, where the anchor motifs show. A flat or shifted length profile points at co-purified peptides or a length filter set too wide. The length table is collapsed.

Filters and components

Filters · Peptide length and Modification on mhcquant_peptides, which also narrow the length profile and the motif heatmap through the project links.

Section What it holds Signature at a glance 4 cards Length signature 2 advanced visualizations Anchor motifs 1 advanced visualization Length table (collapsed) Peptides per length and sample

Immunopeptidome · Which peptides do conditions share, and which proteins do they come from?

The distinct sequences by condition sharing, the peptides per source protein, the protein intensity and the source proteins per peptide. Then the UpSet of the conditions each sequence was identified in, and the source proteins by the peptides they give against their intensity; a click selects the protein. Peptides private to one condition are the candidates for condition-specific presentation: check their support in the peptide record first. The peptide and protein tables are collapsed, each with a record card for the selected row.

Filters and components

Filters · Condition sharing on peptide_condition_sharing and a Peptides per protein range on mhcquant_source_proteins.

Section What it holds Peptides at a glance 4 cards Sharing between conditions 1 advanced visualization Source proteins 1 advanced visualization Peptide detail (collapsed) Identified peptides + a peptide record card Protein detail (collapsed) Source proteins + a protein record card

One condition

On a run with a single condition, the sharing split and the UpSet show a single set.

Tables and scatters select on their entity column: the sample sheet on sample_id, which the links carry to every collection and to the MultiQC panels, and the pinned per-sample summary on sample; the Comet table on raw files (run_id) and the replicate membership table on peptides; the peptide table and the three scatters of Physico-chemical checks on sequence, which also reaches the condition-sharing collection; the source-protein scatter and table on protein; the fragment-ion table on peptide. A pick narrows every tile that reads the same collection or one linked from it, and each record card waits beside its table or scatter for a picked row or point. The length table and the replicate-pair scatter select nothing.

docs.title: Running the pipeline
docs.text:
Depictio reads the output of nf-core/mhcquant, it does not run the pipeline. Run the pipeline first, with quantification and ion annotation if you want the Reproducibility tab and the fragment checks:

nextflow run nf-core/mhcquant -r 3.2.0 \
  --input samplesheet.tsv \
  --fasta proteome.fasta \
  --quantify --annotate_ions \
  --outdir results -profile docker

Then point Depictio at the results, with the samplesheet you started from:

depictio ingest results/ --template nf-core/mhcquant/latest \
  --var METADATA_FILE=samplesheet.tsv --var GROUP_COL=Condition

See nf-co.re/mhcquant/usage for full pipeline documentation.

docs.title: Required data structure
docs.text:
Point depictio ingest at the directory holding the pipeline output. Depictio scans recursively and matches on file name.

<DATA_ROOT>/
├── input/
│   └── samplesheet.tsv                        # the hub (METADATA_FILE default): ID, Sample, Condition, ReplicateFileName
├── <Sample>_<Condition>.tsv                   # one FDR-filtered peptide table per sample
├── multiqc/multiqc_data/
│   └── multiqc.parquet                        # mhcquant custom-content sections
├── intermediate_results/
│   ├── comet/*_pin.tsv                        # Comet PSMs per raw file, before rescoring
│   └── ion_annotations/*_matching_ions.tsv    # optional, --annotate_ions
└── pipeline_info/
    ├── params_*.json
    └── *software*versions*.yml

The replicate intensities are the intensity_<k> columns of the peptide tables, present only with --quantify. The mzTab exports, the OpenMS XML intermediates and the spectral library are not read.

docs.title: Validation runs
docs.text:
The template was validated against the AWS megatest of the 3.2.0 release (results-6ec12c97f7889a3e1f09ab89930723045c6bac68, test_full profile: a PRIDE immunopeptidomics dataset of two samples with three raw replicates each, one sample per condition), and the screenshots above come from it. With one sample per condition, the sharing UpSet on that run is dominated by private peptides. megatest.yaml lists the tables-only subset the template needs, and the download script also places the vendored samplesheet under input/:

bash depictio/projects/nf-core/mhcquant/3.2.0/download_test_data.sh /tmp/mhcquant_test
depictio ingest /tmp/mhcquant_test --template nf-core/mhcquant/latest \
  --var GROUP_COL=Condition

Do not pass --project when ingesting: the dashboard is attached to the project by name, so renaming it breaks a later depictio dashboard import. Re-ingesting accumulates dashboards, so delete the project before repeating a run.

docs.title: Nanopore RNA-seq
docs.text:
Nanopore RNA-seq

Nanopore long-read QC, minimap2 alignment and Bambu gene and transcript quantification, with the DESeq2 and DEXSeq results the pipeline computes on top of them.

nf-co.re GitHub

Experimental Pipeline version 3.0.0 latest

The nanoseq template follows a Nanopore RNA-seq run from the basecalled reads to the genes and isoforms that differ between conditions:

  • Overview: the run in four key figures, live findings and four figures, each linked to the tab that explains it
  • Data & QC: FastQC and samtools panels from the reprocessed MultiQC report, NanoStat's length and quality per library with the Nx and quality ladders, and what minimap2 placed with its identity, depth and indel spectrum
  • Expression: what Bambu counted and whether the libraries group by condition or by preparation, the genes DESeq2 calls between the conditions, and the transcripts DEXSeq finds shifting their share of their gene
Live showcase nf-core/nanoseq, nf-core test data Open

The persistent Sample filters (condition, library, library preparation, flow-cell run, source replicate) sit in the left panel, and the template's links carry a pick to NanoStat, the samtools distributions, the melted Bambu counts and the MultiQC panels alike. The DESeq2 and DEXSeq results carry no sample column, so the filters do not narrow them.

nanoseq 3.0.0 writes no MultiQC parquet

The release ships MultiQC 1.11, which writes multiqc_data.json only, and Depictio reads multiqc.parquet (MultiQC 1.31 and later). Reprocess the run's own tool outputs once before ingesting; the parquet lands in multiqc/multiqc_data/, where the template looks for it:

python -m depictio.dev_scripts.multiqc_reprocess --src <outdir> --dest <outdir>

The design is a variable

nanoseq names every sample <group>_R<replicate>, and the template recovers only those two fields from the name. The condition and the three confounders the dashboard offers beside it (library preparation, source replicate, flow-cell run) come from an optional design table passed as METADATA_FILE. Without it, the condition is the samplesheet group and the confounders read unknown.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Point at a finished runFrom the pipeline itself (v1.10.0+) 
depictio ingest /path/to/nanoseq_results \
  --template nf-core/nanoseq/latest

The results directory is the only thing you have to pass. The hub of the dashboard is the samplesheet the run validated, pipeline_info/samplesheet.valid.csv, one row per library. To bring your own design, add the table and name the factor the run compares:

depictio ingest /path/to/nanoseq_results \
  --template nf-core/nanoseq/latest \
  --var METADATA_FILE=/path/to/sample_metadata.tsv \
  --var GROUP_COL=condition
Variable Default Role METADATA_FILE none Optional design table (TSV), one row per sample (or samplesheet group), one column per factor METADATA_ID_COL first column The design table's id column GROUP_COL first factor column The factor carried as condition; columns named protocol, source_replicate and run_id feed the three confounder filters 
depictio config nextflow --install     # once per machine
nextflow run nf-core/nanoseq -r 3.0.0 -profile docker --outdir results

No depictio ingest, and no template named: the pipeline ingests its own output directory when it finishes and resolves this template from its own manifest. The MultiQC reprocess above still applies to a 3.0.0 run. See Nextflow trigger.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
The template reads the validated samplesheet, the reprocessed MultiQC report, NanoStat's summaries, the samtools stats files of the minimap2 alignments, Bambu's gene and transcript matrices and the DESeq2 and DEXSeq result tables. Bambu publishes feature by sample matrices, so catalog recipes melt them into one row per sample and feature; that is what lets the sample picker reach the counts. When Bambu's row labels are GTF attribute strings, the recipes extract the ENSG or ENST id and promote the biotype to its own filterable column.

Self-adapting layout

The dashboard adapts to whatever the run actually produced: components bound to pruned or unparsed data collections are hidden, tabs left with no real visualizations are dropped entirely, and the remaining components are re-packed so there are no empty rows.

Pipeline nf-core/nanoseq 3.0.0 Template 2.1.0 Updated 1 Nov 2026

docs.title: Template variables
docs.text:
Variables you provide when running the template: DATA_ROOT is the results directory given to depictio ingest, the others are set with --var NAME=value:

Variable Required Description DATA_ROOT ✓ Root directory containing nanoseq output (bambu/, fastqc/, minimap2/, nanoplot/, pipeline_info/) plus the reprocessed multiqc/multiqc_data/multiqc.parquet. METADATA_FILE — Optional design table (TSV): sample name (or samplesheet group) in METADATA_ID_COL, one column per factor. GROUP_COL becomes the condition; columns named protocol, source_replicate and run_id feed the library preparation, source replicate and flow-cell run filters; other factors are carried as extra columns. METADATA_ID_COL — Design table id column. Auto-detected as the first column. GROUP_COL — Design table factor the run compares, carried as the condition column. Auto-detected as the first factor column of METADATA_FILE. GENOME — UCSC name of the assembly the run aligned to (hg38, hg19, mm10): the axis and gene lane of the genome browser. TRACKS_URI — s3:// or https:// folder holding the run's results (the folder DATA_ROOT mirrors), to read the genome-browser tracks (coverage bigWig, long-read BAM) in place instead of uploading them from DATA_ROOT. Without it the tracks collection uploads whichever of those files DATA_ROOT holds.

Auto-detected (set from the run's metadata / params.json; the route flags drive Conditional routes below): GROUP_COL_DISPLAY, ANNOTATION_COLS

docs.title: Dashboard tabs
docs.text:
One dashboard: the Overview, then six child tabs in two groups, read as a funnel from the raw reads to the genes and isoforms that differ between conditions. Each tab below carries the same icon and colour the dashboard gives it, so the page and the app read alike.

Group Tabs Data & QC MultiQC, Reads, Alignment Expression Quantification, Gene expression, Isoform usage

Each child tab opens with a short intro and a strip of four cards, then at most three open sections; tables and details follow, collapsed. The persistent Sample filters (condition, library, then the library preparation, flow-cell run and source replicate) sit in the left panel and narrow every tab with a sample column through the sample hub. DESeq2 and DEXSeq compare the conditions once over the whole run: their result tables carry no sample column, so the sample filters do not narrow the Gene expression tab or the DEXSeq tiles of Isoform usage. The Sample sheet, the library design table, is pinned, collapsed, to the bottom of every child tab. The template also has a Locus tab that embeds a genome browser, opened on the transcript picked in the DEXSeq results, with the run's coverage and read tracks.

Overview MultiQC Reads Alignment Quantification Gene expression Isoform usage

Nanopore long reads, from QC to the genes and isoforms that differ.

A short hero links the run's provenance: nanoseq writes no params.json, so the dialog holds the software versions. About this dashboard says how the two filter levels work, The run lists facts read from the data (libraries, conditions, library preparations, reads), and Pipeline walks the five steps from QC to isoforms, each linked to the version of its tool and its tab. The findings are live values: they follow the filters. The DESeq2 row counts one call per tested annotation entry, as the key figure and the volcano do; the Gene expression tab counts the distinct genes.

Filters and components

Filters · the left panel starts collapsed. Key figures and Findings each have their own filter bar (the condition and the library): each narrows its own section only.

Section What it holds Top Hero, About this dashboard, The run, Pipeline Key figures 4 headline cards: libraries by condition, read length N50, reads placed, DESeq2 calls up and down Findings Live result rows, then 4 figures: length against quality per library, the library PCA, the DESeq2 volcano and the DEXSeq volcano How to read this dashboard The tabs by group, each with its question

Data & QC · Did every library sequence and align as expected?

MultiQC panels only, from the reprocessed report. Open: general statistics, FastQC sequence counts and quality histograms, samtools flagstat and the mapped reads per contig. The other FastQC panels, then the samtools percentages and XY counts, are collapsed. The NanoStat panels are left out: the Reads tab draws the NanoStat summary and its quality ladder from the data, and the Alignment tab the samtools summary.

Filters and components

Filters · the pinned sample filters narrow its panels.

Section What it holds QC overview 5 MultiQC panels FastQC details (collapsed) 6 MultiQC panels samtools details (collapsed) 2 MultiQC panels

Data & QC · How long and how good are the reads of each library?

NanoPlot's summary of each library's raw reads. The reads basecalled, the median read length N50, the median mean read quality (libraries against Q10, failing under Q7) and the median share of reads at Q10 or above. Then mean read length against mean quality, one point per library sized by its yield (nanoseq publishes no per-read table), with the record of the clicked library beside it. The two ladders sit side by side: the Nx ladder recomputed from the samtools read-length histogram, N50 marked, and the share of reads above each Phred floor, Q10 marked. The NanoStat and per-floor tables are collapsed.

Filters and components

Filters · a Mean read quality at least floor and a Read length N50 range on nanostats.

Section What it holds Reads at a glance 4 cards Length and quality 2 advanced visualizations: length against quality and the Library record Ladders 2 advanced visualizations: the Nx ladder and the reads above each quality floor Read tables (collapsed) NanoStat summary, Yield per quality floor

Data & QC · How much of each library aligned, and how accurately?

minimap2 alignments as samtools stats reads them, one summary per library. The median share of reads placed, the median per-base identity (100 minus the mismatch rate per aligned base), the reads mapped and the supplementary alignments, the long-read signal of chimeras. Then the coverage depth distribution, one curve per library, and the indel length spectrum beside the aligned read lengths. The indel spectrum has no legend, as two curves per library pass eight entries: hover a curve for its name. The distributions table is collapsed.

Filters and components

Filters · a Library picker on samtools_stats_sections.

Section What it holds Alignment at a glance 4 cards Coverage 1 advanced visualization Indels and read lengths 2 advanced visualizations: the indel length spectrum and the aligned read lengths Alignment table (collapsed) Alignment distributions

Expression · Do the libraries group by condition, or by preparation?

Bambu's counts per library. The reads assigned by condition, the median genes detected, the median protein-coding share and the median share of the 50 top genes. Then the PCA on log CPM over the 500 most variable genes and the Spearman correlation heatmap, full width with library ids on both axes. The libraries should group by condition; a split by preparation or flow-cell run is a confounder. Collapsed: the 100 most variable genes, row-standardised; depth against complexity, the libraries by preparation and by flow-cell run and the gene expression per library; then the tables.

Filters and components

Filters · Gene biotype and a log2(CPM + 1) range on bambu_counts_gene_long; the biotype also narrows the variable-gene heatmap.

Section What it holds Libraries at a glance 4 cards Sample structure 1 advanced visualization (PCA) Sample correlation 1 advanced visualization (heatmap) Most variable genes (collapsed) 1 advanced visualization (heatmap) Libraries and counts (collapsed) 1 advanced visualization (depth against complexity), 2 cards, Gene expression per library Quantification tables (collapsed) Per-library readings, Correlation matrix, Gene counts per library

Expression · Which genes differ between the two conditions?

DESeq2 on Bambu's gene counts, once over the whole run, so the sample filters do not narrow this tab. The significant genes, ranked up and down, the median log2 fold change of the up calls and of the down calls, each on its own card so neither cancels the other, and the strongest significance against the 5% FDR. Then one tile with three views of the same rows, switched from its View control: the volcano, an MA plot from the mean expression and a QQ plot of the raw p-values, without point labels (the labels are Ensembl ids). The twenty largest fold changes follow, signed. The 200 best-measured rows are collapsed.

Filters and components

Filters · Adjusted p-value, log2 fold change and log2 mean expression ranges and Gene biotype, all on deseq2_results. There is no direction filter: it would empty one of the two direction cards.

Section What it holds Calls at a glance 4 cards Volcano 1 advanced visualization with volcano, MA and QQ views Largest effects 1 advanced visualization Best-measured genes (collapsed) Best-measured DESeq2 rows

Expression · Which transcripts change their share of their gene?

DEXSeq on Bambu's transcript counts: whether a transcript is used more or less relative to its gene's other transcripts, once over the whole run. The transcripts tested against a 5% gene-level q-value, the median usage gain and the median usage loss, each on its own card, and the reads on isoforms by condition. Then the change in usage against the gene-level q-value, with a QQ view and no MA view (DEXSeq writes no mean intensity), and the per-library transcript shares of the top DEXSeq genes, each bar summing to 100% of its gene's reads. The transcript expression per library, the isoform structures and the tables are collapsed.

Filters and components

Filters · Gene biotype and a log2(CPM + 1) range on bambu_counts_transcript_long.

Section What it holds Usage at a glance 4 cards Usage volcano 1 advanced visualization with volcano and QQ views Usage per library Transcript usage per library, top DEXSeq genes Isoform expression (collapsed) Transcript expression per library Isoform structures (collapsed) 1 advanced visualization Isoform tables (collapsed) DEXSeq usage results, Transcript counts per library

The isoform structures need Bambu's extended annotation

The isoform lane view reads bambu/extended_annotations.gtf, which a quantification-only run does not write; without it the view is dropped. nanoseq publishes no splice-junction table, so there is no sashimi view.

Every per-library plot (length against quality, the ladders, the coverage, indel and read-length curves, the PCA, depth against complexity) and every per-library table selects on the library, which the sample hub links to every sample-keyed collection, so a pick narrows the rest of the tab. The length against quality scatter drives the library record card, which waits for a pick. The DEXSeq usage table selects on feature_id, which narrows the other tiles of dexseq_results. The gene and transcript count tables and the DESeq2 table do not select: their feature ids link to no other collection.

docs.title: Running the pipeline
docs.text:
Depictio reads the output of nf-core/nanoseq, it does not run the pipeline. Run the pipeline first:

nextflow run nf-core/nanoseq -r 3.0.0 \
  --input samplesheet.csv \
  --protocol cDNA \
  --quantification_method bambu \
  --outdir results -profile docker

Then regenerate the MultiQC report as a parquet and point Depictio at the results:

python -m depictio.dev_scripts.multiqc_reprocess --src results/ --dest results/
depictio ingest results/ --template nf-core/nanoseq/latest

DESeq2 and DEXSeq need at least two conditions in the samplesheet; a run with one condition leaves the Gene expression and Isoform usage tabs empty. See nf-co.re/nanoseq/usage for full pipeline documentation.

docs.title: Required data structure
docs.text:
Point depictio ingest at the directory holding the pipeline output. Depictio scans recursively and matches on file name, so the DESeq2 and DEXSeq tables are found under bambu/ or stringtie2/ alike.

<DATA_ROOT>/
├── pipeline_info/
│   ├── samplesheet.valid.csv            # the hub: one row per library
│   └── software_versions.yml
├── multiqc/multiqc_data/
│   └── multiqc.parquet                  # written by the reprocess step
├── fastqc/*.zip                         # raw MultiQC inputs
├── nanoplot/fastq/<sample>/
│   └── *NanoStats.txt                   # length and quality summary
├── minimap2/samtools_stats/
│   └── *.bam.{stats,flagstat,idxstats}
├── bambu/
│   ├── counts_gene.txt                  # feature x sample matrices
│   ├── counts_transcript.txt
│   ├── extended_annotations.gtf         # optional: isoform lanes
│   ├── deseq2/deseq2.results.txt
│   └── dexseq/dexseq.results.txt
└── input/sample_metadata.tsv            # optional: METADATA_FILE, anywhere you like

docs.title: Validation runs
docs.text:
The template was validated against the AWS megatest of the 3.0.0 release, results-1e60482a2c4621234393a6eef8e9a104309c20ae: the SG-NEx A549 and K562 cell lines, direct cDNA and cDNA libraries, three replicates each. That run writes no pycoQC, fusion or variant-calling outputs, so the template reads none. Its design table is vendored in the template as input/sample_metadata.tsv, and the screenshots above come from that run:

bash depictio/projects/nf-core/nanoseq/3.0.0/download_test_data.sh /tmp/nanoseq_test
python -m depictio.dev_scripts.multiqc_reprocess --src /tmp/nanoseq_test --dest /tmp/nanoseq_test
mkdir -p /tmp/nanoseq_test/input
cp depictio/projects/nf-core/nanoseq/3.0.0/input/sample_metadata.tsv /tmp/nanoseq_test/input/
depictio ingest /tmp/nanoseq_test --template nf-core/nanoseq/latest \
  --var METADATA_FILE=/tmp/nanoseq_test/input/sample_metadata.tsv

Do not pass --project when ingesting: the dashboard is attached to the project by name, so renaming it breaks a later depictio dashboard import. Re-ingesting accumulates dashboards, so delete the project before repeating a run.

docs.title: Nascent transcription
docs.text:
Nascent transcription

Nascent RNA over a time course, from run-on reads to responding genes: library quality, the response class of each gene, how each time point moves from the baseline, and the strand-specific signal along the genome.

nf-co.re GitHub

Experimental Pipeline version 2.3.0 latest

The nascent template follows an nf-core/nascent run from run-on libraries (GRO-seq, PRO-seq) to the genes and genomic windows that respond over a time course:

  • Overview: the run in four key figures, live findings and four figures, each linked to the tab that explains it
  • Library QC: reads in genes, genes detected and strand balance of each library, in time order
  • Gene dynamics: induced and repressed genes, by the phase of their peak, with the genes that move most
  • Sample similarity: how far each time point has moved from the baseline
  • Genome signal: the strand-specific signal along the genome, linked to a genome browser
  • Signal dynamics: the 250 kb windows that gain or lose signal over time
Live showcase nf-core/nascent, nf-core test data Open

The persistent sample filters (group, library, time point) sit in the left panel and narrow every tab; a pick reaches the per-library collections by sample and the per-gene and per-window calls by the time point of their peak.

Without replicates, a call is a rule

A gene or window is called induced or repressed when its peak change against the baseline is at least twofold and at least two time points move that way. Time courses are rarely replicated, so this is a fold-change rule on consecutive time points, not a statistical test: read a gene's trajectory before trusting its class.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Point at a finished runFrom the pipeline itself (v1.10.0+) 
depictio ingest /path/to/nascent_results \
  --template nf-core/nascent/latest \
  --var METADATA_FILE=/path/to/design.tsv

The results directory is the only required value. nascent publishes neither a sample sheet nor a design table; the optional design gives each library its hours. Without it, a library id ending in a duration (<name>_30min, <name>_2h) still gets its time point, and a library with neither drops out of the time-course panels while its QC stays on Library QC.

Variable Default Role METADATA_FILE unset (reference: {DATA_ROOT}/input/design.tsv) design table: the library id in sample, the hours in TIME_COL, a time_point label and any factor TIME_COL time_h design column holding each library's hours GROUP_COL first factor column of the design column the dashboard groups and filters libraries by TRACKS_URI unset s3:// or https:// folder holding the run's results: the browser reads the bigWigs in place instead of uploading them from DATA_ROOT GENOME hg38 UCSC assembly of the genome tracks' axis and gene lane 
depictio config nextflow --install     # once per machine
nextflow run nf-core/nascent -r 2.3.0 -profile docker --outdir results

No depictio ingest, and no template named: the pipeline ingests its own output directory when it finishes and resolves this template from its own manifest. See Nextflow trigger. The trigger passes no --var, so put a design table at results/input/design.tsv before the run if the library ids do not carry their duration.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
The template reads the featureCounts gene matrix, the strand coverage written as bedGraph and bigWig, and the run parameters. The strand bedGraphs (4 to 10 million intervals each on a human genome) are never ingested whole: two recipes stream them into 250 kb windows and per-library totals. The bigWigs are range-read by the browser for the region in view. The BAMs, the dreg.bedGraph, the QC reports and the transcript identification outputs are not read, and the template has no MultiQC tab.

On the time axis, log2(1 + hours) keeps the first hour from taking a few pixels. The baseline is the earliest time point, and the later ones are split into Early, Mid and Late by rank. An expressed gene has at least 10 reads in at least half of the libraries. A library keeps one colour on every tab, a ramp along the time course (the later, the darker).

Self-adapting layout

The dashboard adapts to whatever the run actually produced: components bound to pruned or unparsed data collections are hidden, tabs left with no real visualizations are dropped entirely, and the remaining components are re-packed so there are no empty rows. A run without the strand coverage drops Genome signal and Signal dynamics.

Pipeline nf-core/nascent 2.3.0 Template 2.0.0 Updated 1 Nov 2026

docs.title: Template variables
docs.text:
Variables you provide when running the template: DATA_ROOT is the results directory given to depictio ingest, the others are set with --var NAME=value:

Variable Required Description DATA_ROOT ✓ Root directory of one nascent run (quantification/, coverage_graphs/, pipeline_info/). METADATA_FILE — Optional design table (TSV): library id in a column named sample (or the first column), the hours of each library in TIME_COL, a time_point label, and any factor. Enables the group filter and colours. METADATA_ID_COL — Design table library-id column. Auto-detected as the first column; defaults to 'sample'. GROUP_COL — Design column the dashboards group, colour and filter libraries by. Auto-detected as the first factor column of METADATA_FILE. TIME_COL — Design column holding each library's time in hours. Without it (or without a design table) the time is read off a library id ending in a duration (30min, 2h, 1d). GENOME — UCSC name of the assembly the run aligned to (--genome; hg38, mm10): the axis and gene lane of the genome tracks. TRACKS_URI — s3:// or https:// folder holding the run's results (the folder DATA_ROOT mirrors), to read the genome-browser bigWigs in place instead of uploading them from DATA_ROOT.

Auto-detected (set from the run's metadata / params.json; the route flags drive Conditional routes below): GROUP_COL_DISPLAY, ANNOTATION_COLS

docs.title: Data collections
docs.text:
20 data collections — 10 required 10 optional · 3 direct 17 derived.

Origin tells you whether a collection is real pipeline data or a reshape of it: direct = a pipeline output (scanned, or a recipe that reads raw files); derived = a recipe that reshapes one or more direct collections into the layout a visualization needs (no new measurement). Reads shows what produces it: a recipe .py transform, or a raw file scanned off disk. (A direct collection can still have a recipe — one that merely parses/cleans the raw file; derived means the recipe reshapes another collection.)

docs.title: Dashboard tabs
docs.text:
One dashboard: the Overview, then five child tabs in two groups, read from the quality of each library to where along the genome transcription changes. Each tab below carries the same icon and colour the dashboard gives it, so the page and the app read alike.

Group Tabs Data & QC Library QC Time course Gene dynamics, Sample similarity, Genome signal, Signal dynamics

Each child tab opens with a short intro and a strip of four cards, then at most three open sections; tables follow, collapsed. The Sample sheet is pinned, collapsed, to the bottom of every child tab.

Overview Library QC Gene dynamics Sample similarity Genome signal Signal dynamics

Nascent transcription over a time course, from run-on reads to responding genes.

Hero, About and run cards and a five-step pipeline flow. Four key figures: the libraries, the reads in genes, the responsive genes and the strand skew (pass, warn and fail against 10 and 15 points). Four findings, each with a highlight, the third naming the chromosome whose share of the signal moves most against its baseline.

Data & QC · Does each library have the depth and balance to be read?

Reads in genes and genes detected per library in time order, against their median (a bar under half the typical depth is shallow; a click narrows the other tiles). The plus-strand share per library against the even split, with the balanced band (40 to 60%) shaded, and the hotspot, off-chromosome and mitochondrial shares. The gene-count and strand tables are collapsed.

Time course · Which genes change transcription over the time course, and when?

The median trajectory of each response class with its quartile band, the ten genes that move most, and the forty most dynamic genes as a heatmap in time order. A response class is a direction with the phase of the peak (Induced early to Repressed late). The call per gene and the value per time point are collapsed.

Time course · How far has each time point moved from the baseline?

The library correlation matrix, a PCA of the libraries coloured by phase, and the correlation of each time point with the baseline and with the previous one. A course moves along the first components in time order: a library off that line is a candidate outlier rather than biology.

Time course · Where along the genome is nascent transcription read?

The binned signal, one thin lane per library, linked to a genome browser with the plus and minus bigWigs: brush a region or type one and the browser zooms to it. The cards follow the region in view, and the lanes and tracks are coloured along the time course. Below, each chromosome's share of the signal against its baseline share, per time point. The lanes are on log2 of the signal, so the ribosomal DNA hotspot does not tower over everything.

Time course · Which genomic windows gain or lose nascent signal over time?

The gene rule applied to the comparable 250 kb windows, so a change outside annotated genes shows too: the windows that change (rising or falling), by phase of the peak, the forty windows that change most as a heatmap, and the median course of each trend. The window table is collapsed.

The gene and window trajectories (and so the median curves and the heatmaps) follow the calls in scope, not the picked time points, so each keeps its whole course. The baseline never peaks: picking only the baseline library leaves no gene or window in scope.

docs.title: Running the pipeline
docs.text:
Depictio reads the output of nf-core/nascent, it does not run the pipeline. Run the pipeline first:

nextflow run nf-core/nascent -r 2.3.0 \
  --input samplesheet.csv \
  --outdir results \
  -profile docker

Then point Depictio at the results, with the design table that gives the hours:

depictio ingest results/ \
  --template nf-core/nascent/latest \
  --var METADATA_FILE=design.tsv

See nf-co.re/nascent/usage for full pipeline documentation.

docs.title: Required data structure
docs.text:
Point depictio ingest at the directory holding the pipeline output. Depictio scans recursively and matches on file name.

<DATA_ROOT>/
├── input/
│   └── design.tsv                              # --var METADATA_FILE (optional, not published)
├── pipeline_info/
│   ├── params_*.json
│   └── *software*versions*.yml
├── quantification/gene/<group>.featureCounts.txt
└── coverage_graphs/
    ├── <sample>.{plus,minus}.bedGraph          # streamed into 250 kb windows
    └── <sample>.{plus,minus}.bigWig            # range-read by the genome browser

docs.title: Validation runs
docs.text:
The repository ships download_test_data.sh, which fetches the subset of nf-core's AWS megatest run that the template needs and copies the vendored sample sheet and design table into input/:

bash depictio/projects/nf-core/nascent/2.3.0/download_test_data.sh \
  /tmp/nascent_test
depictio ingest /tmp/nascent_test \
  --template nf-core/nascent/latest \
  --var METADATA_FILE=/tmp/nascent_test/input/design.tsv

The run is s3://nf-core-awsmegatests/nascent/results-7d4fe61975015f652c271886e661764b05cfd3bf/, the 2.3.0 test_full profile: one GRO-seq time course of 11 single-end libraries, 0 h to 72 h. The download is about 5.2 GB, 4.8 GB of it the strand bedGraphs. That run did not finish its transcript identification and wrote no MultiQC report, which is why the template has no Transcripts or MultiQC tab.

docs.title: Cancer Genomics
docs.text:
Cancer Genomics

Tumor genomes from the WiGiTS toolkit: sequencing QC, purity and ploidy, copy number, structural variants, the driver catalog, somatic and protein-level variants, and immune context.

nf-co.re GitHub

Experimental Template version 3.0.0 latest

The oncoanalyser template reads the tables the Hartwig Medical Foundation WiGiTS toolkit writes for each tumor, from sequencing QC to the protein changes and neoepitopes of its variants:

  • Overview: the run in four key figures, live findings and four figures, each linked to the tab that explains it
  • Data & QC: BamTools coverage and insert sizes, and QSEE's verdict on each check
  • Tumor profile: purity and ploidy, CUPPA's tissue of origin, COSMIC signatures and the HRD probability
  • Copy number and structural variants: PURPLE's copy-number profile, gene-level events, and LINX's rearrangements and fusions
  • Drivers and variants: the driver catalog, somatic small variants, and protein changes on the sequence and on a predicted structure
  • Immune context: HLA alleles, candidate neoepitopes and telomere length
Live showcase nf-core/oncoanalyser, nf-core test data Open

Tables only

The template reads the tools' tables and the PURPLE somatic VCF. It reads no BAM and no MultiQC report (the pipeline writes none), so it has no MultiQC tab. Isofox, PEACH, CIDER, ORANGE and the virus tables are not read yet.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Point at a finished runFrom the pipeline itself (v1.10.0+) 
depictio ingest /path/to/oncoanalyser_results \
  --template nf-core/oncoanalyser/latest

The pipeline outdir is what you pass: one <group_id>/ directory per tumor, plus pipeline_info/. oncoanalyser does not publish the samplesheet it ran on, so the template reads input/samplesheet.csv under that directory by default. Copy your --input sheet there, or name it. A sheet you name makes the CLI guess the id and group columns from its header, so pin them:

depictio ingest /path/to/oncoanalyser_results \
  --template nf-core/oncoanalyser/latest \
  --var METADATA_FILE=/path/to/samplesheet.csv \
  --var METADATA_ID_COL=sample_id \
  --var GROUP_COL=sample_class
Variable Default Role METADATA_FILE {DATA_ROOT}/input/samplesheet.csv The samplesheet the run started with GROUP_COL sample_class Sheet column the dashboard groups samples by. The default is sample_type and sequence_type joined, e.g. tumor_dna GENOME hg38 UCSC name of the assembly: hg38 for GRCh38_hmf, hg19 for GRCh37_hmf. It sets the chord diagram, the genome track and its gene lane 
depictio config nextflow --install     # once per machine
nextflow run nf-core/oncoanalyser -r 3.0.0 -profile docker \
  --mode wgts --genome GRCh38_hmf --input samplesheet.csv --outdir results

No depictio ingest, and no template named: the pipeline ingests its own output directory when it finishes and resolves this template from its own manifest. See Nextflow trigger. The trigger passes no --var, so put a copy of the samplesheet at results/input/samplesheet.csv before the run, and ingest by hand for a --genome GRCh37_hmf run.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
The template reads the per-tumor tables of PURPLE, LINX, BamTools, QSEE, CUPPA, SIGS, CHORD, LILAC, TEAL and Neo, and PURPLE's somatic VCF, of which it keeps the PASS calls. Every output sits under <group_id>/<tool>/, so a cohort run is a set of group directories side by side, and each recipe globs for its files. The protein changes come from the PAVE annotation of the VCF: the three-letter residues of each HGVS protein change become a residue number and one-letter amino acids. A driver row from LINX is kept only when PURPLE has no row for the same tumor, gene and driver type, so LINX's disruptions are added without doubling the reported drivers.

Optional tools drop their tiles

CUPPA, SIGS, CHORD, LILAC, TEAL, Neo and QSEE can be excluded with --processes_exclude, and a targeted (panel) run skips several of them. A run without them skips those collections at ingest, and the dashboard drops the tiles that bind them: the Findings row and the Pipeline step that cite them, a section whose tiles all go, and the Immune context tab when LILAC, Neo and TEAL are all missing. Without QSEE only the QC verdicts and the QSEE table go.

Pipeline nf-core/oncoanalyser 3.0.0 Template 2.1.0 Updated 1 Nov 2026

docs.title: Template variables
docs.text:
Variables you provide when running the template: DATA_ROOT is the results directory given to depictio ingest, the others are set with --var NAME=value:

Variable Required Description DATA_ROOT ✓ oncoanalyser output directory (one / sub-directory per tumor, plus pipeline_info/). METADATA_FILE — The samplesheet the run was started with (--input: group_id, subject_id, sample_id, sample_type, sequence_type, filetype, filepath). Defaults to input/samplesheet.csv under DATA_ROOT. METADATA_ID_COL — Samplesheet id column. oncoanalyser fixes it to sample_id, the name every per-sample output file carries. GROUP_COL — Samplesheet column the dashboard groups and filters samples by. Defaults to sample_class (sample_type and sequence_type joined, e.g. tumor_dna), which the sample hub derives. GROUP_COL_DISPLAY — Reader-facing label of GROUP_COL, used in filter and card titles. GENOME — Genome build of the run (UCSC name): hg38 for GRCh38_hmf, hg19 for GRCh37_hmf. Sets the chromosome ring, the locus views and their gene lane. TRACKS_URI — s3:// or https:// folder holding the run's outdir (the one with a / sub-directory per tumor), to read the genome-browser tracks (PURPLE's VCFs and the BAMs) in place instead of uploading them from DATA_ROOT. Without it the tracks collection uploads whichever of those files DATA_ROOT holds.

docs.title: Data collections
docs.text:
23 data collections — 15 required 8 optional · 20 direct 3 derived.

Origin tells you whether a collection is real pipeline data or a reshape of it: direct = a pipeline output (scanned, or a recipe that reads raw files); derived = a recipe that reshapes one or more direct collections into the layout a visualization needs (no new measurement). Reads shows what produces it: a recipe .py transform, whose name links to its source on GitHub, or a raw file scanned off disk. (A direct collection can still have a recipe — one that merely parses/cleans the raw file; derived means the recipe reshapes another collection.)

docs.title: Dashboard tabs
docs.text:
One dashboard: the Overview, then eight child tabs in three groups, read as a funnel from the sequencing to the tumor's genome and then to its variants. Each tab below carries the same icon and colour the dashboard gives it, so the page and the app read alike.

Group Tabs Data & QC Sequencing QC Genome Tumor profile, Copy number, Structural variants Variants Drivers, Small variants, Protein changes, Immune context

Each child tab opens with a short intro and a strip of four cards, then at most three open sections; tables and record cards follow, collapsed. The persistent Sample filters (sample class, sample, analysis group) sit in the left panel and narrow every tab through the samplesheet links. The Sample sheet is pinned, collapsed, to the bottom of every child tab. The Structural variants and Small variants tabs each embed a genome browser with the tumor's calls and reads.

Overview Sequencing QC Tumor profile Copy number Structural variants Drivers Small variants Protein changes Immune context

Tumor genomes, from the reads to purity, copy number, drivers, variants and immune context.

A short hero links the run parameters. About this dashboard says how the two filter levels work, The run lists the samples, analysis groups, mode, genome and purity fit, and Pipeline walks six steps (align, fit, link, call, classify, type), each linked to its settings and its tab. The findings are live values and follow the filters: the leading signature's share of SNVs, genes lost and gained, structural variants by their commonest resolved event, and somatic calls per megabase. A run without CUPPA and SIGS loses the signature finding.

Filters and components

Filters · the left panel starts collapsed. Key figures and Findings each have their own filter bar (sample class and sample id): each narrows its own section only.

Section What it holds Top Hero, About this dashboard, The run, Pipeline Key figures 4 headline cards: samples, tumor purity, reported drivers, mean coverage Findings Live result rows, then 4 figures: the signature shares, the copy-number profile, the structural variant chord diagram and the allele frequency histogram How to read this dashboard The tabs by group, each with its question

Data & QC · Is the sequencing deep and clean enough for the calls?

BamTools' summary and QSEE's checks. The mean coverage, reads per sample, the highest duplicate share and the lowest share at 30x or more. Then the cumulative coverage and the insert size distribution, one curve per sample, and QSEE's PASS, WARN and FAIL verdicts per tool. The BamTools summary with a library record and the QSEE check table are collapsed.

Genome · How pure is the tumor, and what kind of tumor is it?

PURPLE's fit and the classifiers around it. Purity, ploidy, mutations per Mb and microsatellite indels. Then CUPPA's cancer-type probability per classifier as a heatmap, the share of SNVs per COSMIC signature beside CHORD's HRD probability and the SNVs allocated, and purity against ploidy with one point per tumor. The PURPLE fit table with a tumor record and the CUPPA and CHORD tables are collapsed.

Section What it holds Tumor at a glance 4 cards Tissue of origin 1 advanced visualization: the CUPPA heatmap Mutational processes Share of SNVs per mutational signature, 2 cards Purity and ploidy 1 advanced visualization Tumor detail (collapsed) PURPLE fit per tumor, Tumor record Reference tables (collapsed) CUPPA probabilities, CHORD prediction

Genome · Which regions are gained or lost, and in which genes?

Segments, the median segment copy number, genes in view and the LOH share of the genome. Then PURPLE's copy-number profile along the genome (log2 of copy number over 2, with the B-allele frequency underneath) and the lowest against the highest copy number per gene. Events follow PURPLE's cut-offs: AMP when the lowest copy number is above three times the ploidy, DEL below 0.5 copies, LOH when the minor allele is below 0.5 copies, and PARTIAL_* when only part of the gene qualifies. The tab opens with the event filter on whole and partial amplifications and deletions so the gene scatter stays readable; clearing it adds the genes with LOH or no change. The gene table with a gene record is collapsed.

Filters and components

Filters · Gene copy-number event on purple_gene_copy_number and Chromosome on purple_cnv_segments.

Section What it holds Copy number at a glance 4 cards Copy-number profile 1 advanced visualization Gene copy number 1 advanced visualization Gene detail (collapsed) Copy number per gene, Gene record

Genome · Which rearrangements shaped the genome, and which fusions follow?

LINX's clustered rearrangements and fusion calls. Structural variants, SV clusters, the median junction copy number and candidate fusions. Then a chord diagram of the breakend pairs beside the SVs per resolved event, and the kept and lost exons per fusion beside the fusions per reading frame. The pipeline writes no transcript model, so exon spans are drawn in exon units along the fused transcript, from the fused and total exon counts of each partner. The fusion table with a fusion record and the SV table are collapsed.

Filters and components

Filters · Resolved event and SV type on linx_svs, and Fusion phase on linx_fusions.

Section What it holds Structural variants at a glance 4 cards Rearrangement landscape 1 advanced visualization: the chord diagram, and SVs per resolved event Fusion structure 1 advanced visualization: the exon layout, and Fusions per reading frame Fusion detail (collapsed) Candidate fusions, Fusion record Structural variant tables (collapsed) Structural variants

Variants · Which genes drive this tumor, and how?

PURPLE's driver catalog, with LINX's disruptions added. Driver entries, oncogenes and suppressors, biallelic entries and the median driver likelihood. Then an oncoplot of driver genes by tumor and driver type beside the entries per gene role, and the likelihood per driver type. The tab opens with Report status on REPORTED so the oncoplot stays readable on a whole-genome catalog; clearing it adds the unreported entries. The driver table with a driver record is collapsed.

Filters and components

Filters · Driver type, Gene role, Origin and Report status on purple_drivers.

Section What it holds Drivers at a glance 4 cards Driver landscape 1 advanced visualization: the oncoplot, and Entries per gene role and driver type Driver likelihood Driver likelihood per driver type Driver detail (collapsed) Driver catalog, Driver record

Variants · How many somatic variants are there, and how clonal?

PASS calls of PURPLE's somatic VCF, with the gene, effect and HGVS change from PAVE's canonical transcript. Somatic calls, coding calls, the median purity-adjusted allele frequency and the median variant copy number. Then their histograms (a variant type keeps one colour on every tile) and every call along the genome, with a gene lane. The variant table with a variant record is collapsed.

Filters and components

Filters · Coding effect, Variant type and a Purity-adjusted allele frequency range on purple_somatic_variants.

Section What it holds Variants at a glance 4 cards Clonality Purity-adjusted allele frequency, Variant copy number Along the genome 1 advanced visualization Variant detail (collapsed) Somatic small variants, Variant record

Variants · Which proteins change, and where on the protein and its structure?

Protein changes, proteins hit, changes at known hotspots and the median allele frequency. Then a scatter of the genes with a change (highest purity-adjusted allele frequency against PURPLE's driver likelihood, sized by change count, coloured by worst effect) beside the predicted structure of the picked gene over its written sequence, and a full-width lollipop of its changes. Click a gene on the scatter and the other two follow it; click a residue in one and it is marked in the others, red on the structure. Without a pick the views open on the protein with the most changes, and the Protein filter drives them too. The change table with a record is collapsed.

The structure tile needs the resolver

The pipeline predicts no structure. The 3D structure tile looks the picked gene up by its symbol (UniProt, then the AlphaFold DB model), which needs DEPICTIO_STRUCTURE_RESOLVER_ENABLED=true on the server (it is off by default; see the structure resolver). With it off the tile says the lookup is disabled, and the scatter, the lollipop and the table keep working. A change whose reference residue disagrees with the model is listed, not drawn.

Filters and components

Filters · Protein (a single pick) and Coding effect on purple_protein_changes.

Section What it holds Protein changes at a glance 4 cards Protein view 3 advanced visualizations: the gene scatter, the structure and the lollipop Protein change detail (collapsed) Protein changes, Protein change record

Variants · Which HLA alleles does the tumor keep, and what could they present?

LILAC's HLA alleles, Neo's candidate neoepitopes and TEAL's telomere length. HLA alleles, candidate neoepitopes, their median expression and telomere length. Then the tumor copy number per HLA allele beside the telomere length per sample, and neoepitope expression against variant copy number beside the neoepitopes per source event. The neoepitope table with a record and the HLA allele and telomere tables are collapsed. The tab is dropped when LILAC, Neo and TEAL are all missing.

Filters and components

Filters · HLA gene on lilac_alleles and Neoepitope source on neo_neoepitopes.

Section What it holds Immune context at a glance 4 cards HLA and telomeres Tumor copy number per HLA allele, Telomere length per sample Neoepitopes 1 advanced visualization, Neoepitopes per source event Neoepitope detail (collapsed) Candidate neoepitopes, Neoepitope record Immune reference tables (collapsed) HLA alleles, Telomere length

The sample sheet selects on sample_id, and the sample links carry the pick to every collection. A driver pick narrows the protein changes to its genes, and a gene picked in the copy-number table or scatter narrows the driver catalog. Each record card sits beside the table that drives it and opens on the selected row.

docs.title: Running the pipeline
docs.text:
Depictio reads the output of nf-core/oncoanalyser, it does not run the pipeline. Run the pipeline first; its --input sheet has one row per input file with group_id, subject_id, sample_id, sample_type and sequence_type:

nextflow run nf-core/oncoanalyser -r 3.0.0 \
  --mode wgts \
  --genome GRCh38_hmf \
  --input samplesheet.csv \
  --outdir results -profile docker

Then point Depictio at the results, with the samplesheet the run started with:

depictio ingest results/ \
  --template nf-core/oncoanalyser/latest \
  --var METADATA_FILE=samplesheet.csv \
  --var METADATA_ID_COL=sample_id \
  --var GROUP_COL=sample_class

See nf-co.re/oncoanalyser/usage for full pipeline documentation.

docs.title: Required data structure
docs.text:
Point depictio ingest at the pipeline outdir. Depictio scans recursively and matches on file name; every tumor-level file is named after the tumor's sample_id, which is the key the sample hub links on.

<DATA_ROOT>/
├── input/samplesheet.csv                          # not published by the pipeline: copy it here, or --var METADATA_FILE
├── pipeline_info/
│   ├── params*.json
│   └── *software*versions*.yml
└── <group_id>/                                    # one directory per tumor
    ├── purple/
    │   ├── *.purple.{purity.tsv,qc,cnv.somatic.tsv,cnv.gene.tsv,somatic.vcf.gz}
    │   └── *.driver.catalog.*.tsv
    ├── linx/
    │   ├── somatic_annotations/*.linx.{svs,clusters,fusion,breakend}.tsv
    │   └── {somatic,germline}_annotations/*.driver.catalog.tsv
    ├── bamtools/<sample>/*.bam_metric.{summary,coverage,frag_length}.tsv
    ├── qsee/*.qsee.status.tsv.gz                  # optional
    ├── cuppa/*.cuppa.vis_data.tsv                 # optional
    ├── sigs/*.sig.allocation.tsv                  # optional
    ├── chord/*.chord.prediction.tsv               # optional
    ├── lilac/*.lilac.tsv                          # optional
    ├── teal/*.teal.tellength.tsv                  # optional
    └── neo/scorer/*.neo.neoepitope.tsv            # optional

docs.title: Validation runs
docs.text:
The template was validated against the AWS megatest of the 3.0.0 release, results-7c74c87a43749952b38c9a18915947570f0595a0, on its test_full profile: one WGTS subject, a tumor and normal DNA pair plus tumor RNA. The full run is 272 GB, almost all of it BAMs. megatest.yaml lists the tables-only subset the template needs, about 33 MB, and the script copies the samplesheet under input/. The screenshots above come from that run:

bash depictio/projects/nf-core/oncoanalyser/3.0.0/download_test_data.sh /tmp/oncoanalyser_test
depictio ingest /tmp/oncoanalyser_test --template nf-core/oncoanalyser/latest

Do not pass --project when ingesting: the dashboard is attached to the project by name, so renaming it breaks a later depictio dashboard import. Re-ingesting accumulates dashboards, so delete the project before repeating a run.

docs.title: Pairwise Genome Alignment
docs.text:
Pairwise Genome Alignment

Query genomes aligned to one target with LAST: how much of the target each genome covers and at what identity, how far it has diverged, the contiguity and gaps of the query assemblies, and where the long alignments land.

nf-co.re GitHub

Experimental Template version 3.0.4 latest

The pairgenomealign template follows a run that aligns every genome of its samplesheet (the queries) to one target genome, from the query assemblies to where the long alignments land on the target:

  • Overview: the run in four key figures, live findings and four figures, each linked to the tab that explains it
  • Data & QC: the MultiQC report, and the contiguity, size, composition and scaffolding gaps of each query assembly
  • Alignment: the share of the target each genome covers and the identity of its one-to-one alignment, with the scoring parameters last-train fitted
  • Divergence: Kimura distance, transition bias and the 12-class substitution spectrum of every pair
  • Synteny: the long alignments of one query on a ring shared with the target (needs the PSL export)
Live showcase nf-core/pairgenomealign, nf-core test data Open

Summaries, not alignments

The MAF alignments are gigabytes per pair and are not read: the template reads the small per-pair summaries LAST writes next to them. The Synteny tab needs the PSL export (--export_aln_to psl); without it the tab is dropped at import and the other tabs are untouched.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Point at a finished runWith a design tableFrom the pipeline itself (v1.10.0+) 
depictio ingest /path/to/pairgenomealign_results \
  --template nf-core/pairgenomealign/latest

The results directory is the only thing you have to pass. Every per-pair output is named <target>___<query>, and the query genome is the join key.

depictio ingest /path/to/pairgenomealign_results \
  --template nf-core/pairgenomealign/latest \
  --var METADATA_FILE=genome_metadata.tsv \
  --var GROUP_COL=clade

The samplesheet carries only the genome id and its FASTA, so the design is an optional TSV: the genome id in a sample column (or the first column) and one column per factor. GROUP_COL picks the factor the filters and colours use, the first by default. A run with --skip_assembly_qc needs --var SKIP_ASSEMBLY_QC=true.

depictio config nextflow --install     # once per machine
nextflow run nf-core/pairgenomealign -r 3.0.4 -profile docker --outdir results

No depictio ingest, and no template named: the pipeline ingests its own output directory when it finishes and resolves this template from its own manifest. See Nextflow trigger.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
The template reads, per genome pair, the one-to-one identity summary (*.o2o.tsv), the substitution matrix with its distance estimates (*.o2o.matrix.txt) and the fitted scoring parameters (*.train.tsv); per query assembly, the assembly-scan JSON and the seqtk poly-N BED; and the optional PSL export. A genome hub, one row per query genome, joins them with the design table: every filter starts from it, and a selection made on an alignment or assembly tile narrows the hub and through it every other tab.

Self-adapting layout

The dashboard adapts to whatever the run actually produced: components bound to pruned or unparsed data collections are hidden, tabs left with no real visualizations are dropped entirely, and the remaining components are re-packed so there are no empty rows. Without the PSL export the Synteny tab, its pipeline step and its findings row go. With --skip_assembly_qc the assembly statistics go, while the gap views read from the BEDs stay.

Pipeline nf-core/pairgenomealign 3.0.4 Template 1.1.0 Updated 1 Nov 2026

docs.title: Template variables
docs.text:
Variables you provide when running the template: DATA_ROOT is the results directory given to depictio ingest, the others are set with --var NAME=value:

Variable Required Description DATA_ROOT ✓ Root directory of one pairgenomealign run (alignment/, assemblyscan/, cutn/, multiqc/, pipeline_info/). METADATA_FILE — Optional design table (TSV): genome id in a column named sample (or in the first column), one column per factor such as a clade. Enables the design filters and grouping. METADATA_ID_COL — Design table genome-id column. Auto-detected as the first column; defaults to 'sample'. GROUP_COL — Design column the dashboards group and filter genomes by. Auto-detected as the first factor column of METADATA_FILE. SKIP_ASSEMBLY_QC — Set (--var SKIP_ASSEMBLY_QC=true) for a run with --skip_assembly_qc: no assemblyscan/ reports, so the assembly statistics collection is pruned.

Auto-detected (set from the run's metadata / params.json; the route flags drive Conditional routes below): GROUP_COL_DISPLAY, ANNOTATION_COLS

docs.title: Data collections
docs.text:
10 data collections — 3 required 7 optional · 9 direct 1 derived.

Origin tells you whether a collection is real pipeline data or a reshape of it: direct = a pipeline output (scanned, or a recipe that reads raw files); derived = a recipe that reshapes one or more direct collections into the layout a visualization needs (no new measurement). Reads shows what produces it: a recipe .py transform, whose name links to its source on GitHub, or a raw file scanned off disk. (A direct collection can still have a recipe — one that merely parses/cleans the raw file; derived means the recipe reshapes another collection.)

Tag Origin Type Reads Status metadata direct Table file {METADATA_FILE} optional last_split_identity direct Table recipe last/split_identity.py required last_split_matrix direct Table recipe last/split_matrix.py optional last_train_params direct Table recipe last/train_params.py optional last_synteny_links direct Table recipe last/synteny_links.py optional assemblyscan_stats direct Table recipe assemblyscan/stats.py optional seqtk_cutn_gaps direct Table recipe seqtk/cutn_gaps.py optional seqtk_cutn_gap_lengths direct Table recipe seqtk/cutn_gap_lengths.py optional genomes derived Table recipe nf-core/pairgenomealign/genomes.py required multiqc_data direct MultiQC file (?:.*/)?multiqc(?:/[^/]+)?/multiqc_data/multiqc.parquet$ required

docs.text:
Rows are data collections; columns are the variables you set or params.json flags auto-detected from the run. Each filled cell is the effect of setting that variable; an empty cell means that variable leaves the collection unchanged. (8 collections are unaffected by any variable — present on every run.)

+ included− removed⇄ repointed

docs.title: Dashboard tabs
docs.text:
One dashboard: the Overview, then five child tabs in two groups, read as a funnel from the query assemblies to where the long alignments land on the target. Each tab below carries the same icon and colour the dashboard gives it, so the page and the app read alike.

Group Tabs Data & QC MultiQC, Assemblies Genome alignment Alignment, Divergence, Synteny

Each child tab opens with a short intro and a strip of four cards, then at most three open sections; tables and record cards follow, collapsed. The persistent Sample filters (design group and query genome) narrow every tab through the genome hub.

Overview MultiQC Assemblies Alignment Divergence Synteny

Pairwise genome alignment, from the query assemblies to identity, divergence and synteny.

A short hero links the run parameters. The run lists the genome count and target, the seed and soft-masking, the strand, the mismap limit and the export format, and Six steps from genomes to alignments walks check, train, align, compare, link and report, each linked to its parameters and its tab. The findings are live values that follow the filters.

Filters and components

Filters · the left panel starts collapsed. Key figures and Findings each have their own filter bar (the design group and the query genome): each narrows its own section only.

Section What it holds Key figures 4 headline cards: query genomes (split by group), genome size, target covered, percent identity Findings Live result rows (identity with target coverage, K80 distance with transition bias, N50 with the share of sequences over 1 Mb, synteny links with their matching bases), then 4 figures: the contiguity scatter, identity against coverage, the fitted gap costs and the saturation scatter

Data & QC · What does the MultiQC report say about the alignments?

MultiQC panels only. The report holds custom content: the one-to-one identity and the fitted parameters of every genome pair, then the contig length statistics and the base content of every query assembly. The pair id reaches the alignment panels by prefix and the genome the assembly panels directly, so the pinned sample filters narrow them.

Filters and components

Filters · Report scope (Report row) narrows the panels to selected report rows, next to the pinned sample filters.

Section What it holds Alignment sections 2 MultiQC panels: one-to-one alignment identity, fitted alignment parameters Assembly sections 2 MultiQC panels: contig length statistics, base content

Data & QC · How contiguous is each query assembly, and where are its gaps?

Sequences against N50 of each assembly on log axes, sized by length, then the gap length matrix: one row per assembly, the lengths of its runs of N on a log10 scale across and the share of its runs in each bin as the colour. A fixed scaffolding filler is one dark cell, and a dotted line marks the common 100 bp one.

Filters and components

Filters · Assembly scope: N50 (bp) and Sequences, both range sliders.

Section What it holds Assemblies at a glance 4 cards: N50, sequences over 1 Mb, assembly length, GC content Contiguity 1 advanced visualization, Sequences against N50 per assembly; a lasso on it narrows every tab Scaffolding gaps 1 advanced visualization, Gap lengths per assembly Assembly tables (collapsed) Assembly statistics, Assembly gaps

Genome alignment · How much of the target does each genome cover, at what identity?

Percent identity is the identical columns over all alignment columns, gaps included. Every genome is placed by target coverage and identity, with the record of the picked genome beside it (alignment, divergence and assembly in one card), then the gap cost last-train fitted against the identity of its training alignments. A closer genome gets a higher cost.

Filters and components

Filters · Alignment scope: Percent identity and Target covered (%), both range sliders.

Section What it holds Alignment at a glance 4 cards: percent identity, target covered, aligned length, gap opening cost Identity and coverage Target coverage against identity per genome, with the Picked genome record beside it Fitted parameters 1 advanced visualization, Fitted gap cost against training identity Alignment tables (collapsed) One-to-one alignment per query genome, Fitted scoring parameters per genome pair

Genome alignment · How far has each genome diverged from the target?

The K80 distance is substitutions per site on the aligned A, C, G and T columns. The transition bias is plotted against the raw distance, one point per pair sized by its blocks (the ratio falls as multiple hits saturate the transitions), beside the substitution spectrum: the share of each of the 12 directed substitutions per genome, scaled per column and clustered by row.

Filters and components

Filters · Divergence scope: K80 distance, a range slider.

Section What it holds Divergence at a glance 4 cards: K80 distance, transitions over transversions, alignment blocks, deletions in the query Saturation 1 advanced visualization, Transition bias against divergence Substitution spectrum 1 advanced visualization, Substitution spectrum per genome Divergence tables (collapsed) Substitutions and distances per genome pair

Genome alignment · Where do the long alignments of each query land on the target?

Only with a PSL export, which keeps up to 2000 alignments per pair. Target and query sequences share the ring: a chord joins the two loci of an alignment, its width the matching bases and its colour the orientation. The ring reads one query genome, and its picker is always selected, so it holds the first query until another is picked.

Filters and components

Filters · Synteny scope: Query genome (a single pick) and Orientation.

Section What it holds Synteny at a glance 4 cards: links, matching bases, identity of the links, span of the links Synteny ring 1 advanced visualization, Synteny between the target and the picked query; click chords to select their alignments Link tables (collapsed) Alignments behind the chords

docs.title: Running the pipeline
docs.text:
Depictio reads the output of nf-core/pairgenomealign, it does not run the pipeline. Run the pipeline first, with the PSL export if you want the Synteny tab:

nextflow run nf-core/pairgenomealign -r 3.0.4 \
  --input samplesheet.csv \
  --target target_genome.fasta \
  --export_aln_to psl \
  --outdir results -profile docker

Then point Depictio at the results. The run writes a MultiQC parquet, so no reprocess step is needed:

depictio ingest results/ --template nf-core/pairgenomealign/latest

See nf-co.re/pairgenomealign/usage for full pipeline documentation.

docs.title: Required data structure
docs.text:
Point depictio ingest at the directory holding the pipeline output. Depictio scans recursively and matches on file name. The *.o2o.tsv summaries and the MultiQC report are mandatory; the rest is optional.

<DATA_ROOT>/
├── input/
│   └── genome_metadata.tsv                     # optional design table (--var METADATA_FILE)
├── pipeline_info/                              # params_*.json, *software*versions*.yml
├── multiqc/multiqc_data/multiqc.parquet        # custom content sections
├── alignment/
│   ├── <target>___<query>.o2o.tsv              # mandatory: identity and coverage per pair
│   ├── <target>___<query>.o2o.matrix.txt       # substitutions and distances (Divergence)
│   ├── <target>___<query>.train.tsv            # fitted scoring parameters (Alignment)
│   └── <target>___<query>.psl.gz               # only with --export_aln_to psl
├── assemblyscan/*.json                         # absent with --skip_assembly_qc
└── cutn/*.bed                                  # runs of N per query assembly

docs.title: Validation runs
docs.text:
The repository ships download_test_data.sh, which fetches the subset of nf-core's AWS megatest run that the template needs:

bash depictio/projects/nf-core/pairgenomealign/3.0.4/download_test_data.sh /tmp/pga_test

The run is s3://nf-core-awsmegatests/pairgenomealign/results-8ee09a1cdc920fc90cd62358952045e5019e1fe0/, the 3.0.4 test_full profile: 34 query genomes aligned to one target assembly. The run is 42.8 GB, almost all of it alignments; the manifest keeps the per-pair summaries, about 20 MB. It ran without the PSL export, so the Synteny tab is dropped on this data. The script also copies the samplesheet and the design table the template ships (clade, divergence_mya) to input/.

Then run Depictio against it:

depictio ingest /tmp/pga_test \
  --template nf-core/pairgenomealign/latest \
  --var METADATA_FILE=/tmp/pga_test/input/genome_metadata.tsv \
  --var GROUP_COL=clade
