docs.title: Protein annotation
docs.text:
Protein annotation

Protein sequences filtered, searched for domains in four HMM libraries and InterProScan, given a predicted secondary structure, and folded on demand one protein at a time.

nf-co.re GitHub

Experimental Template version 1.1.0 latest

The proteinannotator template follows an nf-core/proteinannotator run from the input FASTA files to one protein's structure, reading each tool's own files and joining them per residue, per domain, per protein and per sample:

  • Overview: the run in four key figures, live findings and four figures, each linked to the tab that explains it
  • Data & QC: what the length and duplicate filter removed, and how much of each protein the databases describe
  • Domains: hits from Pfam, FunFam, NMPFamsDB, MetagRoot and InterProScan in one table, drawn along each chain, and where the databases agree
  • Secondary structure: the S4PRED helix, strand and coil calls per residue, with the domains that cover them
  • Structure: one protein in 3D, coloured by its best domain, linked residue by residue to its sequence track
Live showcase nf-core/proteinannotator, nf-core test data Open

Folding needs the structure resolver and sends the sequence out

The pipeline predicts no 3D structure. The Structure tab folds the picked protein from its sequence through the structure resolver, which is off by default: an administrator sets DEPICTIO_STRUCTURE_RESOLVER_ENABLED=true on the server. Folding sends the protein sequence to ESMFold on Meta's ESM Atlas (api.esmatlas.com), and ESMFold folds at most 400 residues. With the resolver off, or for a longer protein, the tile says why it is empty and the rest of the dashboard is unaffected.

Grouping needs a design table

The pipeline's samplesheet has only id and fasta, so a design is always an extra table, passed with --var METADATA_FILE. Without one, the group filters, the Samples card and the design table are pruned, and every tile bound to the per-sample summary keeps working.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Point at a finished runFrom the pipeline itself (v1.10.0+) 
depictio ingest /path/to/proteinannotator_results \
  --template nf-core/proteinannotator/latest

The results directory is the only thing you have to pass. To group and filter samples, add a design table: the sample id in the first column (or a column named sample), then one column per factor.

depictio ingest /path/to/proteinannotator_results \
  --template nf-core/proteinannotator/latest \
  --var METADATA_FILE=/path/to/design.tsv
Variable Default Role METADATA_FILE unset design table; enables the group filters, the Samples card and the design table GROUP_COL first factor column design column the dashboard groups and filters by SKIP_INTERPROSCAN unset set for a --skip_interproscan run: drops the InterProScan collections and the step that cites them SKIP_S4PRED unset set for a --skip_s4pred run: drops the Secondary structure tab; the residue table keeps its sequence and domains 
depictio config nextflow --install     # once per machine
nextflow run nf-core/proteinannotator -r 1.1.0 -profile docker --outdir results

No depictio ingest, and no template named: the pipeline ingests its own output directory when it finishes and resolves this template from its own manifest. See Nextflow trigger.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
The template reads the SeqFu statistics and the filtered FASTA of qc/, the hmmsearch domain tables of four HMM libraries (Pfam, FunFam, NMPFamsDB, MetagRoot), InterProScan's signature matches and the S4PRED secondary structure. Empty files are normal (InterProScan writes an empty TSV for a sample with no match, hmmsearch a header-only table) and read as no rows. The run's MultiQC report holds only SeqFu sections anchored by sample name, so the template has no MultiQC tab.

  • Protein ids. A protein is the first word of its FASTA header, the id the three tools report. Characters outside A-Za-z0-9._+- become _ in every table, so the S4PRED, domain, residue and protein tables share one entity.
  • Domains. hmmsearch domains are kept at an independent E-value of 0.01 or less, HMMER's own inclusion threshold, and span the envelope coordinates. Weaker hits stay in the collapsed hmmsearch hits section. InterProScan matches are kept as reported.
  • Coverage. A protein's annotated share counts the residues covered by at least one domain once. The best domain, the one with the lowest E-value, names the protein and colours the structure.

Self-adapting layout

The dashboard adapts to whatever the run actually produced: components bound to pruned or unparsed data collections are hidden, tabs left with no real visualizations are dropped entirely, and the remaining components are re-packed so there are no empty rows. A --skip_s4pred run loses the Secondary structure tab and its Overview finding.

Pipeline nf-core/proteinannotator 1.1.0 Template 1.1.0 Updated 1 Nov 2026

docs.title: Dashboard tabs
docs.text:
One dashboard: the Overview, then four child tabs in two groups, read from the sequences that survived the filter to the structure of one of them. Each tab below carries the same icon and colour the dashboard gives it, so the page and the app read alike.

Group Tabs Data & QC Input filtering Annotation Domains, Secondary structure, Structure

Each child tab opens with a short intro and a strip of four cards, then at most three open sections; tables follow, collapsed. The persistent Sample filters sit in the left panel and the Sample sheet (the design table and the per-sample summary) is pinned, collapsed, to the bottom of every child tab. The annotation databases share one palette, and the S4PRED states are fixed: helix, strand and coil.

Overview Input filtering Domains Secondary structure Structure

Protein sequences, filtered, searched for domains and given a predicted secondary structure.

A short hero links the run parameters. About this dashboard says how the two filter levels work, The run lists the samples, the proteins, the length window, the E-value and the InterProScan applications, and Pipeline walks five steps (filter, search, match, predict, fold), each linked to its parameters and its tab. The findings are live values that follow the filters: the median annotated share, the domains and the database that reports most, the commonest predicted state, and the proteins short enough to fold.

Filters and components

Filters · the left panel starts collapsed. Key figures has its own filter bar (group and sample), Findings another (group and database): each narrows its own section only.

Section What it holds Top Hero, About this dashboard, The run, Pipeline Key figures 4 headline cards: samples, proteins, domains, residues in a domain Findings Live result rows, then 4 figures: length against annotated share, the domain architecture, the state shares and one protein along its chain How to read this dashboard The tabs by group, each with its question

Data & QC · Which sequences passed the filter, and how well are they annotated?

The sequences removed, the protein length, the residues kept per sample and the domains per protein. Then the sequences before and after the filter, per sample, and the length against the share of the protein that sits in a domain, one point per protein, whose picked protein opens in a record card beside it. Low points are mostly outside known families. The protein table is collapsed.

Filters and components

Filters · Protein length (residues), Residues in a domain (%) and Annotation status on proteinannotator_proteins.

Section What it holds Filter at a glance 4 cards Filter yield Sequences before and after the filter Annotated share 2 advanced visualizations: the scatter and the Protein record Protein table (collapsed) Proteins

Annotation · Which domains does each protein carry, and do the databases agree?

The domain architecture draws one backbone per protein with its domains from all five databases, coloured by database; a click selects the protein and the span on the residue tables and the family on the domain table, the scatter and the record card. A View control groups proteins by architecture. The architecture, its record card, the protein by database heatmap and the UpSet plot (which databases agree) share one linked view, so they stay side by side. Significance against span separates families from motifs and borderline calls. The domain table and the raw hmmsearch hits are collapsed.

Filters and components

Filters · Database, Family or signature, Significance (-log10 E-value) and Domain span (residues) on proteinannotator_domains.

Section What it holds Domains at a glance 4 cards Architecture and agreement (linked view) 4 advanced visualizations: the architecture, the Domain record, the coverage heatmap and the UpSet Domain calls Significance against span Domain detail (collapsed) Domains hmmsearch hits (collapsed) Bit score against HMM coverage, hmmsearch domain table

Annotation · Which stretches of each protein fold as helix, strand or coil?

The tab shows one protein, the shortest first; its scope banner names it and its sample. The residues S4PRED called, the probability of the called state, and the helix and strand probabilities. Then a linked view stacks the secondary structure ribbon, over the probability of each state with its segment list, on the sequence track, which also draws the domain spans; a brush or a segment pick selects the same residues on both. A stacked bar compares the state shares of the proteins. The residue table is collapsed.

Filters and components

Filters · Protein (always one, opening on the shortest) and Residue window on s4pred_secondary_structure.

Section What it holds Prediction at a glance 4 cards Predicted structure (linked view) 2 advanced visualizations: the ribbon and the sequence track Composition Predicted states per protein Residue table (collapsed) Residues

Annotation · Where do the domains sit on one protein's 3D structure?

The tab shows one protein, the shortest first so that the first one folds. Its scope banner prints its length, domain hits and annotated share. A linked view puts its 3D structure, coloured by best domain over its written sequence, beside the sequence track (state, probability and domain spans), linked residue by residue: a click on a residue in 3D, on a letter of the sequence or a brush on the track selects the same residues in both. A protein over 400 residues cannot be folded: its tile says so, and the Protein length card flags it.

Filters and components

Filters · Protein (always one, opening on the shortest) and Protein length (residues) on proteinannotator_proteins, and Residue window on proteinannotator_residues. The length filter has no default window, so every protein stays in the picker.

Section What it holds Structure at a glance 4 cards: domains, residues in a domain, domains per residue, protein length Structure and domains (linked view) 2 advanced visualizations: the predicted structure and the sequence track Protein summary (collapsed) Protein Residue table (collapsed) Residues

Tables and point views select on entity, the protein id, so a protein picked in one tile is the protein in the others; the domain tiles also select on the family, and the structure and the track on the residue position.

docs.title: Running the pipeline
docs.text:
Depictio reads the output of nf-core/proteinannotator, it does not run the pipeline. Run the pipeline first:

nextflow run nf-core/proteinannotator -r 1.1.0 \
  --input samplesheet.csv \
  --outdir results \
  -profile docker

The samplesheet is id,fasta, one protein FASTA per sample. Then point Depictio at the results, with a design table if you have one:

depictio ingest results/ \
  --template nf-core/proteinannotator/latest \
  --var METADATA_FILE=design.tsv

For a run with --skip_interproscan or --skip_s4pred, add --var SKIP_INTERPROSCAN=true or --var SKIP_S4PRED=true.

See nf-co.re/proteinannotator/usage for full pipeline documentation.

docs.title: Required data structure
docs.text:
Point depictio ingest at the directory holding the pipeline output. Depictio scans recursively and matches on file name; the sample and the database are read off the path.

<DATA_ROOT>/
├── input/
│   └── design.tsv                              # optional, wherever --var METADATA_FILE points
├── pipeline_info/
│   ├── params_*.json
│   └── *software*versions*.yml
├── qc/<sample>/
│   ├── <sample>_{before,after}.tsv             # SeqFu statistics around the filter
│   └── <sample>.fasta                          # the filtered FASTA every later step ran on
├── domain_annotation/<db>/<sample>.domtbl.gz   # hmmsearch, one directory per library
├── functional_annotation/interproscan/<sample>/<sample>.tsv   # optional
└── s4pred/<sample>/ss2/<sequence id>.ss2       # optional

docs.title: Validation runs
docs.text:
The repository ships download_test_data.sh, which fetches the subset of nf-core's AWS megatest run that the template needs and copies the vendored samplesheet and design table into input/:

bash depictio/projects/nf-core/proteinannotator/1.1.0/download_test_data.sh \
  /tmp/proteinannotator_test
depictio ingest /tmp/proteinannotator_test \
  --template nf-core/proteinannotator/latest \
  --var METADATA_FILE=/tmp/proteinannotator_test/input/sample_metadata.tsv

The run is s3://nf-core-awsmegatests/proteinannotator/results-cbf78d471f62d91af666e8c77bcd580b4743c6be/, a development run that reports itself as v1.2.0dev: three single-protein FASTA inputs (two structure-prediction targets and one enzyme) searched against test-sized Pfam, FunFam, NMPFamsDB and MetagRoot libraries, InterProScan with the HAMAP, TIGRFAM and SFLD applications, and S4PRED. The design table's protein_set column was written for the demo.

docs.title: Protein families
docs.text:
Protein families

Protein sequences grouped into families: how the input clustered, the families a run built or extended, and each family's alignment, residue conservation, predicted structure and profile HMM.

nf-co.re GitHub

Experimental Template version 2.5.0 latest

The proteinfamilies template follows an nf-core/proteinfamilies run from the input sequences to one family's profile model, funnel-wise:

  • Overview: the run in four key figures, live findings and four figures, each linked to the tab that explains it
  • Data & QC: the input sequences before and after preprocessing, and the MMseqs2 cluster size distribution per sample
  • Families: the families a run built or extended, their size and conservation, and how close their members sit to the representative
  • Alignment: each family's alignment, residue conservation and predicted structure, and its profile HMM as a sequence logo with the members that matched it
Live showcase nf-core/proteinfamilies, nf-core test data Open

The persistent Sample filters (mode, sample) sit in the left panel and narrow every tab through the samplesheet links.

Structure tiles need the structure resolver

proteinfamilies publishes no structure files. The 3D tiles of the Family alignment and Profile HMM tabs fold the family representative from its sequence through the structure resolver, which is off by default: an administrator sets DEPICTIO_STRUCTURE_RESOLVER_ENABLED=true on the server. The sequence is sent to ESMFold on Meta's ESM Atlas, which folds at most 400 residues. With the resolver off the tile shows an empty state.

Create and update runs

A run either creates families from its input sequences or, given the HMMs and alignments of an existing library, first matches the sequences against those families and extends them. The mode column (create or update) is derived from the samplesheet and is the default grouping. Families an update run extended carry the origin updated, the others new.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Point at a finished runFrom the pipeline itself (v1.10.0+) 
depictio ingest /path/to/proteinfamilies_results \
  --template nf-core/proteinfamilies/latest

The results directory is the only thing you have to pass, with one exception: proteinfamilies reads its samplesheet from --input and does not publish it. The template looks for it at {DATA_ROOT}/input/samplesheet.csv; copy it there, or point to it:

depictio ingest /path/to/proteinfamilies_results \
  --template nf-core/proteinfamilies/latest \
  --var METADATA_FILE=/path/to/samplesheet.csv
Variable Default Role METADATA_FILE {DATA_ROOT}/input/samplesheet.csv the samplesheet the run was started with GROUP_COL mode samplesheet column the dashboard groups and filters samples by; any design column added to the sheet can replace mode GROUP_COL_DISPLAY Mode reader-facing label of GROUP_COL in filters and cards 
depictio config nextflow --install     # once per machine
nextflow run nf-core/proteinfamilies -r 2.5.0 -profile docker --outdir results

No depictio ingest, and no template named: the pipeline ingests its own output directory when it finishes and resolves this template from its own manifest. See Nextflow trigger. The trigger passes no --var, so put a copy of the samplesheet at results/input/samplesheet.csv before the run.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
The template reads the SeqFu statistics of the input, the MMseqs2 cluster size distribution, the family metadata and member rosters, the family alignments, the family HMMs and the hmmalign alignments. Per-family files are laid out <step>/<sample>/<family>.<ext>, so every family collection carries the sample (the directory) and the family (the file name), and the families table carries a family pick to the alignment, residue and member collections. Families an update run extended live under update_families/. The alignment scan reads FAMSA (.aln, the default) and MAFFT (.fas) full alignments alike, and the HH-suite reformatted .fas.gz that a --skip_sequence_redundancy_removal run writes.

Self-adapting layout

The dashboard adapts to whatever the run actually produced: components bound to pruned or unparsed data collections are hidden, tabs left with no real visualizations are dropped entirely, and the remaining components are re-packed so there are no empty rows. A run that published neither the family HMMs (hmm/) nor the hmmalign alignments (full_msa/raw/) loses the logo, the hits lane and the table of members on the model. A run with no update sample has no updated family.

Pipeline nf-core/proteinfamilies 2.5.0 Template 1.1.0 Updated 1 Nov 2026

docs.title: Dashboard tabs
docs.text:
One dashboard: the Overview, then five child tabs in three groups, read as a funnel from the input sequences to one family's profile model. Each tab below carries the same icon and colour the dashboard gives it, so the page and the app read alike.

Group Tabs Data & QC Input & Clustering Families Families, Members Alignment Family alignment, Profile HMM

Each child tab opens with a short intro and a strip of four cards, then at most three open sections; tables and record cards follow, collapsed. The Sample sheet and the family table (Reference tables) are pinned, collapsed, to the bottom of every child tab. The family origin and the conservation class (conserved, intermediate, variable) have fixed colours, so the landscape, the histograms, the track and the structure agree.

Overview Input & Clustering Families Members Family alignment Profile HMM

Protein families, from the input sequences to each family's profile HMM.

A short hero links the run parameters. About this dashboard says how to move through the tabs, The run lists the samples, the clustering tool and identity, the aligner, the seed cluster threshold and the recruiting E-value, and Pipeline walks five steps (cluster, align, model, recruit, prune), each linked to its parameters and its tab. The findings are live values that follow the filters.

Filters and components

Filters · the left panel starts collapsed. Key figures has its own filter bar (mode and sample), Findings another (mode and family origin): each narrows its own section only.

Section What it holds Top Hero, About this dashboard, The run, Pipeline Key figures 4 headline cards: samples, input sequences, families, family members Findings Live result rows, then 4 figures: the initial cluster size distribution, the family landscape, the member scatter and the residue conservation histogram How to read this dashboard The tabs by group, each with its question

Data & QC · How many sequences went in, and how did they cluster?

The SeqFu statistics of the input and the MMseqs2 cluster sizes. The input sequences, the sequences kept after the length filter, gap removal and deduplication, the mean sequence length and the share left as singleton clusters. Then the initial cluster size distribution, one curve per sample on log axes (only clusters above the size threshold seed a family), and the sequences before and after preprocessing. A large drop there points at a length range or duplicate content worth checking.

Then the family landscape, one point per family by size against mean conservation and sized by representative length, with the record of the picked family beside it, and the family size per sample. The predicted structure of the picked family's representative floats over the dashboard: it opens compact, stays on screen on every tab and follows the filters of the tab you read.

Then the identity per family, where a wide box is a family ranging from near copies to distant homologues, and the member scatter, coverage against identity, with the record of the picked member beside it. The member roster is collapsed.

Then two histograms of the representative's residues, by conservation score and by column occupancy, coloured by class. A linked view then holds the predicted structure of the picked family's representative, coloured by conservation, on the left, and the family scatter, the sequence track and the family alignment stacked on the right. docs.title: Running the pipeline
docs.text:
Depictio reads the output of nf-core/proteinfamilies, it does not run the pipeline. Run the pipeline first:

nextflow run nf-core/proteinfamilies -r 2.5.0 \
  --input samplesheet.csv \
  --outdir results \
  -profile docker

The samplesheet is sample,fasta, plus existing_hmms_to_update and existing_msas_to_update for a sample that extends an existing family library. Then point Depictio at the results, naming the samplesheet the pipeline did not publish:

depictio ingest results/ \
  --template nf-core/proteinfamilies/latest \
  --var METADATA_FILE=samplesheet.csv

The run can also write samplesheets for proteinfold and proteinannotator; --skip_proteinfold_samplesheet and --skip_proteinannotator_samplesheet turn them off.

See nf-co.re/proteinfamilies/usage for full pipeline documentation.

docs.title: Required data structure
docs.text:
Point depictio ingest at the directory holding the pipeline output. Depictio scans recursively and matches on file name; the sample and the family are read off the path.

<DATA_ROOT>/
├── input/
│   └── samplesheet.csv                         # --var METADATA_FILE (not published by the pipeline)
├── pipeline_info/
│   ├── params_*.json
│   └── *software*versions*.yml
├── qc/<sample>/<sample>_{before,after}.tsv     # SeqFu statistics of the input
├── mmseqs/initial_clustering/
│   └── *_clustering_distribution_mqc.csv       # cluster size distribution
├── family_reps/<sample>/
│   ├── *_meta_mqc.csv                          # family metadata
│   └── <sample>.tsv                            # member roster
├── full_msa/
│   ├── filtered/{famsa_align,mafft_align,hhsuite_reformat}/<sample>/<family>.{aln,fas}
│   └── raw/hmmer_hmmalign/<sample>/<family>.sto.gz   # optional: logo mapping, hits lane
├── hmm/filtered/<sample>/<family>.hmm.gz       # optional: the profile logo
└── update_families/                            # update samples only, same layout

Only the HMMs and the hmmalign alignments are optional.

docs.title: Validation runs
docs.text:
The repository ships download_test_data.sh, which fetches the subset of nf-core's AWS megatest run that the template needs (files up to 5 MB) and copies the vendored samplesheet into input/:

bash depictio/projects/nf-core/proteinfamilies/2.5.0/download_test_data.sh \
  /tmp/proteinfamilies_test
depictio ingest /tmp/proteinfamilies_test \
  --template nf-core/proteinfamilies/latest

The run is s3://nf-core-awsmegatests/proteinfamilies/results-f8c0b183e59df3d87c38d0f7c4acc6918593f4f5/, the test_full profile: two samples of 50,000 metagenomic protein sequences each, one creating families from scratch and one updating an existing family library before creating new families from its unmatched sequences. The screenshots above come from that run.

docs.title: Protein structure prediction
docs.text:
Protein structure prediction

Protein sequences folded by one or several engines, then scored: how far each model can be trusted, where along the chain it is confident, how domains and chains sit relative to each other, and where the engines agree.

nf-co.re GitHub

Experimental Template version 2.1.0 latest

The proteinfold template reads the models an nf-core/proteinfold run wrote for each target and engine (AlphaFold2 in standard or split-MSA mode, ColabFold, ESMFold, RoseTTAFold All-Atom, ...), and follows them from their scores to the engines' agreement:

  • Overview: the run in four key figures, live findings and four figures, each linked to the tab that explains it
  • Model scores: the pLDDT and pTM of every model, per engine
  • Structure: the picked structure in 3D over its sequence, per-residue confidence, the Ramachandran plot and the alignment it was folded from
  • Predicted error: the predicted aligned error matrix beside the structure, to pick a confident domain
  • Engines comparison: the engines and the models of one target, rank by rank and residue by residue
Live showcase nf-core/proteinfold, nf-core test data Open

The persistent Sample filters (assembly, target, target length) sit in the left panel and narrow every tab through the target hub.

Structures are read from the run, not resolved

The 3D and Ramachandran tiles read the top-ranked PDB that each engine publishes under top_ranked_structures/, so nothing leaves the server and the structure resolver (DEPICTIO_STRUCTURE_RESOLVER_ENABLED) is not used. Those PDBs are required: a run that published none has no structure to open.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Point at a finished runFrom the pipeline itself (v1.10.0+) 
depictio ingest /path/to/proteinfold_results \
  --template nf-core/proteinfold/latest

The results directory is the only thing you have to pass, with one exception: proteinfold does not publish the samplesheet it ran on. The template looks for it at {DATA_ROOT}/input/samplesheet.csv; copy it there, or point to it:

depictio ingest /path/to/proteinfold_results \
  --template nf-core/proteinfold/latest \
  --var METADATA_FILE=/path/to/samplesheet.csv
Variable Default Role METADATA_FILE {DATA_ROOT}/input/samplesheet.csv the samplesheet the run was started with GROUP_COL assembly column the dashboard groups and filters targets by; assembly is derived (single chain or complex), and any samplesheet column beyond id and fasta works GROUP_COL_DISPLAY Assembly reader-facing label of GROUP_COL in filters and cards 
depictio config nextflow --install     # once per machine
nextflow run nf-core/proteinfold -r 2.1.0 -profile docker --outdir results

No depictio ingest, and no template named: the pipeline ingests its own output directory when it finishes and resolves this template from its own manifest. See Nextflow trigger. The trigger passes no --var, so put a copy of the samplesheet at results/input/samplesheet.csv before the run.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
The unit of every structure tile is the entity: one engine's top-ranked structure of one target. Its id is the id the structures collection gives the PDB, <engine>__<target>, with a non-default AlphaFold2 mode between the two, so every per-structure table joins the 3D object without a lookup. The template reads the PDBs (pLDDT sits in the B-factor column), the per-model pLDDT, pTM, ipTM and ipSAE tables, the PAE matrix of the top-ranked model only (_0_ for AlphaFold2 and RoseTTAFold All-Atom, _1_ for ColabFold, which numbers its models from 1) and the integer-coded alignments of the MSA-based engines. Model ranks are renumbered from 1, and the pLDDT bands follow AlphaFold: very high from 90, confident from 70, low from 50, very low below.

ESMFold writes no alignment, no PAE and no TM scores, and single-chain targets write empty ipTM and ipSAE files, which read as no rows. Alignments are capped at 500 rows, and a profile longer than 200 residues is averaged over equal windows. The MultiQC reports repeat the residue table and cannot be bound generically, so the template has no MultiQC tab.

Self-adapting layout

The dashboard adapts to whatever the run actually produced: components bound to pruned or unparsed data collections are hidden, tabs left with no real visualizations are dropped entirely, and the remaining components are re-packed so there are no empty rows. The PAE matrices, the score files and the alignments are optional: a run that wrote no PAE drops the assess step of the Overview pipeline with them.

Pipeline nf-core/proteinfold 2.1.0 Template 1.1.0 Updated 1 Nov 2026

docs.title: Template variables
docs.text:
Variables you provide when running the template: DATA_ROOT is the results directory given to depictio ingest, the others are set with --var NAME=value:

Variable Required Description DATA_ROOT ✓ proteinfold output directory (one directory per engine, e.g. alphafold2/, colabfold/, esmfold/, plus multiqc/ and pipeline_info/). METADATA_FILE — The samplesheet the run was started with (--input: id, fasta, any extra design columns). Defaults to input/samplesheet.csv under DATA_ROOT. METADATA_ID_COL — Samplesheet id column. proteinfold fixes it to id (the target name every output file carries); recorded for auto-detection only. GROUP_COL — Target hub column the dashboard groups and filters targets by. Defaults to assembly (single chain or complex, derived from the structures); any samplesheet column works. GROUP_COL_DISPLAY — Reader-facing label of GROUP_COL, used in filter and card titles.

docs.title: Data collections
docs.text:
11 data collections — 7 required 4 optional · 9 direct 2 derived.

Origin tells you whether a collection is real pipeline data or a reshape of it: direct = a pipeline output (scanned, or a recipe that reads raw files); derived = a recipe that reshapes one or more direct collections into the layout a visualization needs (no new measurement). Reads shows what produces it: a recipe .py transform, whose name links to its source on GitHub, or a raw file scanned off disk. (A direct collection can still have a recipe — one that merely parses/cleans the raw file; derived means the recipe reshapes another collection.)

docs.title: Dashboard tabs
docs.text:
One dashboard: the Overview, then four child tabs in two groups, read from how far a model can be trusted to whether the engines agree. Each tab below carries the same icon and colour the dashboard gives it, so the page and the app read alike.

Group Tabs Data & QC Model scores Structure Structure, Predicted error, Engines comparison

Each child tab opens with a short intro and a strip of four cards, then at most three open sections; tables and record cards follow, collapsed. The Sample sheet (the targets of the samplesheet) is pinned, collapsed, to the bottom of every child tab. The pLDDT bands take AlphaFold's own colours.

Overview Model scores Structure Predicted error Engines comparison

Protein structure prediction, from the sequence to the model each engine builds.

A short hero links the run parameters. About this dashboard says how to move through the tabs, The run counts the targets, engines, models and residues and prints the requested mode, and Pipeline walks six steps (targets, align, fold, score, assess, compare), each linked to its parameters and its tab. The findings are live values that follow the filters: the structures and engines, the median mean pLDDT with the share of residues under 50, the mean PAE and the models ranked.

Filters and components

Filters · the left panel starts collapsed. Key figures has its own filter bar (assembly and target), Findings another (assembly and engine): each narrows its own section only.

Section What it holds Top Hero, About this dashboard, The run, Pipeline Key figures 4 headline cards: targets by assembly, top-ranked structures by engine, mean pLDDT, residues at pLDDT 70 or more Findings Live result rows, then 4 figures: the first structure in 3D, the mean pLDDT per engine, the PAE matrix of the first structure and the top model of each engine per target How to read this dashboard The tabs by group, each with its question

Data & QC · How far can each engine's top-ranked models be trusted?

The models predicted, the mean pLDDT of the top models, the share of residues at pLDDT 70 or more and the pTM of the top models. Then every model's mean pLDDT against its pTM, and the mean pLDDT of every model per engine. pLDDT scores each residue and pTM the whole fold, so a high pLDDT with a low pTM is a set of confident pieces placed loosely. Engines that write no TM score (ESMFold, RoseTTAFold All-Atom) are absent from the scatter and the pTM card.

Filters and components

Filters · Engine and Model rank on proteinfold_models.

Section What it holds Models at a glance 4 cards Confidence and fold quality 1 advanced visualization Engines compared Mean pLDDT of every model, per engine

Structure · Where along each structure is the prediction confident?

The tab reads one target: its Target filter always holds a value and opens on the first. The strip gives the median residue pLDDT, the residues by confidence band, the likely disordered residues and the best mean pLDDT. Then a linked view holds the picked structure in 3D, coloured by pLDDT over its written sequence, on the left. Stacked on the right are a table with one row per engine's top-ranked structure, which picks the structure, the sequence with its pLDDT lane, the pLDDT profile of every engine and the Ramachandran plot of the picked structure (phi and psi computed in the browser, coloured by pLDDT). A click on a residue in 3D, on a letter or a brush on the track selects the same residues in all of them. The alignment the structure was folded from and the residue table are collapsed.

Filters and components

Filters · Target and Residue range on proteinfold_residues.

Section What it holds Confidence at a glance 4 cards Structures and confidence (linked view) Structures of the target, one row per engine, then 4 advanced visualizations: the structure, the sequence track, the Ramachandran plot and the pLDDT per engine Alignment (collapsed) Alignment the structure was folded from Residue table (collapsed) Residues of the structures in scope

A lone query row in the alignment

It is the data, not a filter: the engine found or used no homologs. ESMFold folds without an alignment, so its structure opens the tile on an empty state.

Structure · Which domains and chains does the model place confidently?

The tab reads one structure. The strip gives its mean PAE, the pLDDT of its residues, and the pTM and ipTM of its top-ranked model against AlphaFold's cut-offs (pTM 0.5; ipTM 0.8 and 0.6). Then the PAE matrix beside the same structure in 3D, coloured by pLDDT, and the sequence with its pLDDT lane below. A diagonal brush on the matrix selects a square as a residue range: the structure draws it red and the sequence track shades it, so a confident domain is picked in 3D. Dark blocks off the diagonal are domains or chains placed confidently relative to each other; on a complex the chain boundaries are marked.

Filters and components

Filters · a Structure picker on proteinfold_residues. It always holds a value and does not offer ESMFold's structures, which have no matrix. There is no engine filter: the structure id carries its engine.

Section What it holds Error at a glance 4 cards Error matrix and structure 2 advanced visualizations: the matrix and the structure Domains along the sequence 1 advanced visualization, the sequence track

Structure · Do the engines and their models agree on each target?

The models in scope, split by engine, the median mean pLDDT per model, the weakest model's mean pLDDT against the 70 and 50 cut-offs, and the pTM per model. Then the mean pLDDT of each engine's top-ranked model, the mean pLDDT by model rank, one line per engine (a steep fall from the first model means the ranking was decisive), and the per-residue profile: one curve per engine, the line the top-ranked model and the band the lowest to the highest of its models. A wide band marks residues the engine's models disagree on, and curves that part mark residues the engines disagree on. The models table and its record card are collapsed.

Filters and components

Filters · Target compared (one at a time), Engines compared and Model rank on proteinfold_models.

Section What it holds Models at a glance 4 cards Best model per engine Mean pLDDT of each engine's top-ranked model Rank and agreement Mean pLDDT by model rank, and 1 advanced visualization Model detail (collapsed) Models, Model record

Tables and point views select on entity, the structure id, so a pick narrows the other tiles of its collection and follows the project links to the rest. The three single-unit pickers (the target of Structure and Engines comparison, the structure of Predicted error) always hold exactly one value, so the tiles that show one structure at a time agree on it.

docs.text:
Depictio reads the output of nf-core/proteinfold, it does not run the pipeline. Run the pipeline first:

nextflow run nf-core/proteinfold -r 2.1.0 \
  --input samplesheet.csv \
  --mode alphafold2,colabfold,esmfold \
  --outdir results \
  -profile docker

The samplesheet is id,fasta; extra columns are kept and can become the grouping column. --mode takes one or several engines, and each needs its own databases and weights: see the usage documentation. Then point Depictio at the results, naming the samplesheet the pipeline did not publish:

depictio ingest results/ \
  --template nf-core/proteinfold/latest \
  --var METADATA_FILE=samplesheet.csv

See nf-co.re/proteinfold/usage for full pipeline documentation.

docs.title: Required data structure
docs.text:
Point depictio ingest at the directory holding the pipeline output. Depictio scans recursively and matches on file name; the engine, its AlphaFold2 mode and the target are read off the path.

<DATA_ROOT>/
├── input/
│   └── samplesheet.csv                         # --var METADATA_FILE (not published by the pipeline)
├── pipeline_info/
│   ├── params_*.json
│   └── *software*versions*.yml
└── <engine>[/<mode>]/                          # alphafold2/standard, colabfold, esmfold, ...
    ├── top_ranked_structures/<target>.pdb      # required: pLDDT in the B-factor
    ├── <target>_plddt.tsv                      # per-model pLDDT
    ├── <target>_{ptm,iptm,ipsae}.tsv           # optional; ipTM and ipSAE empty for one chain
    ├── <target>/paes/<target>_0_pae.tsv        # optional; _1_ for colabfold
    └── <target>/<target>_<engine>_msa.tsv      # optional; MSA-based engines only

docs.title: Validation runs
docs.text:
The repository ships download_test_data.sh, which fetches the subset of nf-core's AWS megatest run that the template needs and copies the vendored samplesheet into input/:

bash depictio/projects/nf-core/proteinfold/2.1.0/download_test_data.sh \
  /tmp/proteinfold_test
depictio ingest /tmp/proteinfold_test \
  --template nf-core/proteinfold/latest

The run is s3://nf-core-awsmegatests/proteinfold/results-a414fd1368009500b66761e37e7cde80366a45e9/, a 2.1.0 development run (the 2.0.0 release run is empty): eleven test_full runs gathered under one prefix, AlphaFold2 (standard and split-MSA), ColabFold, ESMFold and RoseTTAFold All-Atom on two monomer targets, and AlphaFold2 multimer and ESMFold on one heterodimer. The script fetches the top-ranked PAE matrix of each engine and target only.

docs.title: DIA proteomics
docs.text:
DIA proteomics

Label-free DIA proteomics, from the spectra to the proteins that change: whether the runs were acquired alike, what each run identified, how completely proteins were quantified, whether replicates agree, and which proteins differ between conditions.

nf-co.re GitHub

Experimental Pipeline version 1.1.1 latest

The quantms template reads the DIA route of an nf-core/quantms run and follows it from the spectra to the proteins that change between conditions:

  • Overview: the run in four key figures, live findings and four figures, each linked to the tab that explains it
  • Acquisition: whether the runs were acquired alike, from the mzML spectrum statistics
  • Identification: the precursors each run identified and their quality, from DIA-NN
  • Proteins: the protein groups quantified, how completely, and how much they vary between runs
  • Reproducibility: whether the runs of a condition agree and the conditions separate
  • Differential abundance: the MSstats contrasts, with the volcano and the calibration of the test
Live showcase nf-core/quantms, nf-core test data Open

The persistent Sample filters (condition, run) sit in the left panel and narrow every tab: the links carry a pick to every run-level table by run_id and to the per-condition tables by condition.

DIA only

quantms quantifies proteins in three modes: data-dependent acquisition with label-free quantification, isobaric labelling and data-independent acquisition (DIA). This template reads the DIA route (DIA-NN and MSstats). The other two write other tables and need their own template.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Point at a finished runFrom the pipeline itself (v1.10.0+) 
depictio ingest /path/to/quantms_results/mode_dia \
  --template nf-core/quantms/latest

The directory to pass is the one holding diannsummary/, msstats/, mzmlstatistics/, sdrfparsing/ and pipeline_info/: that of one mode, which is mode_dia/ for the nf-core megatest. The design is read from sdrfparsing/, so no SDRF is needed; the SDRF only adds its characteristics columns (organism, instrument and so on):

depictio ingest /path/to/quantms_results/mode_dia \
  --template nf-core/quantms/latest \
  --var METADATA_FILE=/path/to/sdrf.tsv
Variable Default Role METADATA_FILE {DATA_ROOT}/input/sdrf.tsv the SDRF the run was started with (optional) GROUP_COL condition column the dashboard groups and filters runs by; leave it at the MSstats condition GROUP_COL_DISPLAY Condition reader-facing label of GROUP_COL in filters and cards 
depictio config nextflow --install     # once per machine
nextflow run nf-core/quantms -r 1.1.1 -profile docker --outdir results

No depictio ingest, and no template named: the pipeline ingests its own output directory when it finishes and resolves this template from its own manifest. See Nextflow trigger.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
The template reads the design quantms parsed from the SDRF, the mzML spectrum statistics, the DIA-NN precursor report and protein-group matrix, and the MSstats comparisons. Derived collections (the run summary, the protein summary, the per-condition statistics, the run projection and the replicate pairs) are recipes over those tables. There is no MultiQC tab: quantms 1.1.1 reports through pmultiqc custom content, which has no multiqc.parquet, so the plots of that report are rebuilt from the result tables.

A call is an Up or Down protein at an adjusted p-value below 0.05 and an absolute log2 fold change of at least one, the dashboard's cut-offs (MSstats reports the adjusted p-value only). The coefficient of variation is taken over the runs of a condition that quantified the group, and needs at least two. The DIA-NN version of this release reports no mass error, so Identification has no mass-accuracy view.

Self-adapting layout

The dashboard adapts to whatever the run actually produced: components bound to pruned or unparsed data collections are hidden, tabs left with no real visualizations are dropped entirely, and the remaining components are re-packed so there are no empty rows. With one condition there is no contrast, and Differential abundance shows empty panels.

Pipeline nf-core/quantms 1.1.1 Template 1.1.0 Updated 1 Nov 2026

docs.title: Template variables
docs.text:
Variables you provide when running the template: DATA_ROOT is the results directory given to depictio ingest, the others are set with --var NAME=value:

Variable Required Description DATA_ROOT ✓ quantms output directory of one mode (the folder holding diannsummary/, msstats/, mzmlstatistics/, sdrfparsing/ and pipeline_info/). For the megatest this is the mode_dia/ folder. METADATA_FILE — The SDRF the run was started with (--input). Optional: the design is already in sdrfparsing/, the SDRF adds its characteristics columns. Defaults to input/sdrf.tsv under DATA_ROOT. METADATA_ID_COL — Hub id column. The quantms hub is keyed on run_id, the raw file name without its extension; this only records that value. GROUP_COL — Hub column the dashboard groups and filters runs by. Defaults to condition, the MSstats condition of the design. GROUP_COL_DISPLAY — Reader-facing label of GROUP_COL, used in filter and card titles.

docs.title: Dashboard tabs
docs.text:
One dashboard: the Overview, then five child tabs in two groups, read as a funnel from the spectra to the proteins that change. Each tab below carries the same icon and colour the dashboard gives it, so the page and the app read alike.

Group Tabs Data & QC Acquisition, Identification Quantification Proteins, Reproducibility, Differential abundance

Each child tab opens with a short intro and a strip of four cards, then at most three open sections; tables and record cards follow, collapsed. The Sample sheet and the Reference tables (the per-run summary) are pinned, collapsed, to the bottom of every child tab.

Overview Acquisition Identification Proteins Reproducibility Differential abundance

Label-free DIA proteomics, from the spectra to the proteins that change.

Hero, About and run cards (runs, conditions, acquisition method, enzyme, tolerances, search database) and a five-step Pipeline (acquire, identify, quantify, compare runs, test). Four key figures: the runs, the protein groups per run, the median variation between replicates (a threshold at 20 %) and the significant proteins. The findings follow the filters, then the run projection, the variation against abundance, the volcano and the p-value histogram.

Data & QC · Were the runs acquired alike?

The MS2 spectra per minute and the median MS2 base-peak intensity per minute, one curve per run, and the share of MS2 spectra by the number of peaks they hold. Runs of one experiment are expected within about 5 % of the median on the gradient and the MS2 rate. The spectra summary is collapsed. Filter: a retention-time window.

Data & QC · How many precursors did each run identify, and how clean are they?

One per-run quality view, the weakest run on top: the deviation from the median of the precursors, the yield per thousand MS2 spectra, the modified share and the missed-cleavage share, coloured by condition. Then the gap between observed and predicted retention time along the gradient, and the peptide length and DIA-NN evidence score per run. The precursor table is collapsed. Filters: modification, charge and peptide length.

Quantification · Which protein groups were quantified, and how completely?

The variation between runs against abundance for every group, with a dashed line at a coefficient of variation of 20 % and the most variable groups labelled by gene. The groups missed in some runs, by how many runs quantified them, and the protein-group table with a record card that links the UniProt entry are collapsed. Filters: detection, peptide support and a variation range.

Quantification · Do the runs of a condition agree, and do the conditions separate?

The run projection (a lasso filters the linked panels), the difference between two runs against their mean for every replicate pair, and the variation within each condition as a violin, where under 20 is tight and over 30 noisy. The clustered run correlation and the per-condition table are collapsed. Filters: replicate pair and a variation range.

Quantification · Which proteins change between conditions, and can the test tell?

The proteins called Up and Down in each contrast, the volcano with its MA and QQ views (dashed lines at an adjusted p of 0.05 and at log2 fold changes of -1 and 1), the p-value histogram and the fold-change histogram. A flat histogram says the test is calibrated and no protein changed enough. The MSstats table and its record card are collapsed. Filters: contrast, direction, effect size and missing values.

The sample sheet selects on run_id, and the protein tables, the variation scatter and the volcano select on protein_group. A pick narrows the other tiles of its collection and of the collections linked from it. A record card waits for a picked row or point.

docs.title: Running the pipeline
docs.text:
Depictio reads the output of nf-core/quantms, it does not run the pipeline. Run the pipeline first, on an SDRF of a DIA experiment:

nextflow run nf-core/quantms -r 1.1.1 \
  --input sdrf.tsv \
  --outdir results \
  -profile docker

See the usage documentation for the DIA options. Then point Depictio at the directory of the DIA results:

depictio ingest results/ --template nf-core/quantms/latest

See nf-co.re/quantms/usage for full pipeline documentation.

docs.text:

bash depictio/projects/nf-core/quantms/1.1.1/download_test_data.sh \
  /tmp/quantms_test
depictio ingest /tmp/quantms_test --template nf-core/quantms/latest

The run is s3://nf-core-awsmegatests/quantms/results-600505011027ab196bb18b1320607468bdae951a/, whose mode_dia/ folder holds four label-free DIA runs of two conditions. It therefore has a single contrast, and the per-contrast views read one. The other two modes of that run (mode_lfq, mode_tmt) are not read.

docs.title: Rare disease
docs.text:
Rare disease

Rare disease analysis of a family, from the alignment to the ranked variants: alignment and coverage QC, pedigree checks, the callset, the GENMOD-ranked variants and their inheritance models, mitochondrial, repeat and mobile element calls, and a genome browser.

nf-co.re GitHub

Experimental Pipeline version 3.1.2 latest

The raredisease template follows an nf-core/raredisease run on a family, usually a trio, from the alignment to the ranked variants:

  • Overview: the run in four key figures, live findings and a leaderboard of the best-ranked variants, each linked to the tab that explains it
  • Data & QC: the MultiQC report, the alignment and coverage numbers per sample, and whether the samples are the family the pedigree says
  • Variants: the callset per sample, the GENMOD-ranked variants with their inheritance models, and the optional mitochondrial and repeat branches
  • Locus: the ranked variants on the genome, with a browser on the calls and alignments
Live showcase nf-core/raredisease, nf-core test data Open

A pick on a sample, a role (proband, father, mother, sibling) or a family in the left panel narrows every per-sample collection, the MultiQC report and the genome browser's tracks.

Roles come from the pedigree

The pipeline publishes its pedigree as a .ped file, so the group the filters use is the role, read from it, and the affected status colours the pedigree figure. A run without the pedigree keys the sample hub on the QC and callset samples, and every role reads Other.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Point at a finished runFrom the pipeline itself (v1.10.0+) 
depictio ingest /path/to/raredisease_results \
  --template nf-core/raredisease/latest

The results directory is the only required value. The run's reference decides the one variable you may need to set:

depictio ingest /path/to/raredisease_results \
  --template nf-core/raredisease/latest \
  --var GENOME=hg38
Variable Default Role GENOME hg19 assembly of the navigator, the karyotype and the browser's tracks: hg19 is the GRCh37 naming, hg38 that of GRCh38 TRACKS_URI unset s3:// or https:// folder holding the run's results: the browser reads the alignments and signal tracks in place instead of uploading them from DATA_ROOT 
depictio config nextflow --install     # once per machine
nextflow run nf-core/raredisease -r 3.1.2 -profile docker --outdir results

No depictio ingest, and no template named: the pipeline ingests its own output directory when it finishes and resolves this template from its own manifest. See Nextflow trigger. The trigger passes no --var, so a GRCh38 run reads on the hg19 axis; ingest it by hand with GENOME=hg38 instead.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
The template reads the pedigree, the Picard and mosdepth QC, the family callset, the VEP-annotated and GENMOD-ranked VCFs (the clinical set is a subset of the research set and is flagged, so no variant is counted twice), the optional mitochondrial, repeat expansion, mobile element and SMN outputs, the MultiQC report and the run parameters. The alignments, the ranked and repeat VCFs and the signal tracks are never loaded as tables: the genome browser opens them through their indexes. peddy, GENS, the germline CNV caller and structural variant calling are not read.

The callset summary, the substitution spectrum and the FILTER breakdown count the calls a sample carries (a genotype with an alternate allele), not the sites of the joint file. A target capture (exome) run fills the hybrid-selection coverage columns instead of the whole-genome ones, and the tiles that read the latter draw a dash.

Self-adapting layout

The dashboard adapts to whatever the run actually produced: components bound to pruned or unparsed data collections are hidden, tabs left with no real visualizations are dropped entirely, and the remaining components are re-packed so there are no empty rows. A run that skipped the mitochondrial branch loses the Mitochondria tab, one without repeat expansion or mobile element calling loses their cards and tables.

Pipeline nf-core/raredisease 3.1.2 Template 1.1.0 Updated 1 Nov 2026

docs.title: Template variables
docs.text:
Variables you provide when running the template: DATA_ROOT is the results directory given to depictio ingest, the others are set with --var NAME=value:

Variable Required Description DATA_ROOT ✓ Root directory of one raredisease run (alignment/, call_snv/, rank_and_filter/, qc_bam/, pedigree/, pipeline_info/). GENOME — UCSC name of the assembly the run was aligned to (hg19 for GRCh37, hg38 for GRCh38): the axis of the Locus tab and the gene track of the browser. TRACKS_URI — s3:// or https:// folder holding the run's results (the one that holds alignment/, rank_and_filter/ and qc_bam/), to read the genome-browser tracks (the ranked VCFs and the alignments) in place instead of uploading them from DATA_ROOT. Without it the tracks collection uploads whichever of those files DATA_ROOT holds.

docs.title: Dashboard tabs
docs.text:
One dashboard: the Overview, then eight child tabs in two groups, read as a funnel from the reads to what the calls and alignments show at one locus. Each tab below carries the same icon and colour the dashboard gives it, so the page and the app read alike.

Group Tabs Data & QC MultiQC, Alignment, Family Variants Callset, Ranked, Mitochondria, Repeats, Locus

Each child tab opens with a short intro and a strip of four cards, then at most three open sections; tables follow, collapsed.

Overview MultiQC Alignment Family Callset Ranked Mitochondria Repeats Locus

Rare disease analysis of a family, from the alignment to the ranked variants.

Hero, About and run cards (genome, analysis type, aligner, caller, VEP cache, skipped tools) and six steps (Align, Call, Rank, Mitochondria, Repeats, Report), each with its settings and its tab. Four key figures: the clinical variants by inheritance model, the top rank score, the samples by role and the mean coverage. The findings are led by the top candidate, then a leaderboard of the eight best-ranked variants and the pedigree.

Data & QC · What does the MultiQC report say about reads and alignments?

General statistics, FastQC counts and fastp filtered reads, then the Picard alignment summary, duplicates, insert size and the coverage histogram. Base quality, adapter content and the mosdepth curves are collapsed.

Data & QC · What do the alignment, coverage and call numbers say, sample by sample?

Reads, aligned share, mean coverage, duplication and the mitochondrial to nuclear depth ratio, and one table of the samples with the record of the picked sample beside it. The contig depth and the full tables are collapsed.

Data & QC · Are the samples the family the pedigree says they are?

The samples by affected status, the parent-child IBS0 share and the sex check. The pedigree figure from the sample sheet (squares male, circles female, filled marks affected) sits beside the opposite homozygous share of every pair of samples, one bar each, coloured by the verdict. The pair table is collapsed.

Variants · How many calls does each sample yield, and how clean are they?

PASS calls, Ts/Tv, het/hom ratio and calls by FILTER value. Ts/Tv and het/hom per sample as two sorted bars with the usual range shaded (a click narrows the dashboard to that sample), and the substitution spectrum folded onto six classes. Ts/Tv is about 2.0 to 2.1 for a genome and 2.8 to 3.0 for an exome. The karyotype of one sample and the allele fraction per sample are collapsed.

Variants · Which variants rank first, and which inheritance model do they fit?

The 50 best candidates as a leaderboard, best first, with the gene and protein change, the inheritance model and impact as badges and the rank score as a bar. Hover for the consequence, frequency, CADD and carriers; a click picks the variant for the record beside it and opens the pedigree filled by genotype. Then the rank score of the 50 best variants, why the 20 best rank (one segment per GENMOD score component) and the genotype of every individual at those variants.

Variants · How heteroplasmic are the mitochondrial calls, and how rare?

Optional branch. Calls by heteroplasmy class, median heteroplasmy, impact and depth, then heteroplasmy along the mitochondrial genome and against the gnomAD frequency. The mitochondrion is not on the navigator's axis, so this tab has no genome view.

Variants · Do any repeat expansions or mobile element insertions stand out?

Optional branches. Repeat calls by status, pathogenic-range calls by inheritance, mobile element insertions by family and SMN calls. One row per repeat locus, each call placed by its repeat count as a multiple of the pathogenic threshold over shaded normal, intermediate and pathogenic zones; insertions per sample by element family. The tables are collapsed.

Variants · What do the calls and alignments show at one locus?

A navigator draws every ranked variant at its position, higher for a higher rank score and coloured by the inheritance model it fits, linked to a genome browser. The browser opens on the span of the 20 best-ranked variants (else the top-ranked one), showing the research VCF, the proband alignment and coverage, the parents' alignments and the ClinVar and dbSNP tracks; the rest is in its track menu. A brush or a typed locus moves the browser, a rank score slider in the left panel narrows the points to the top, and the ranked variants of the region are listed below.

Tables and leaderboards select rows, and a pick narrows the other tiles of its collection and follows the project links to the rest.

docs.title: Running the pipeline
docs.text:
Depictio reads the output of nf-core/raredisease, it does not run the pipeline. Run the pipeline first:

nextflow run nf-core/raredisease -r 3.1.2 \
  --input samplesheet.csv \
  --outdir results \
  -profile docker

The mitochondrial, repeat expansion, mobile element and SMN branches are optional, and the template adapts to the ones that ran. Then point Depictio at the results, naming the assembly the run used if it is GRCh38:

depictio ingest results/ \
  --template nf-core/raredisease/latest \
  --var GENOME=hg38

See nf-co.re/raredisease/usage for full pipeline documentation.

docs.title: Required data structure
docs.text:
Point depictio ingest at the directory holding the pipeline output. Depictio scans recursively and matches on file name.

<DATA_ROOT>/
├── pedigree/<family>.ped                                  # family, parents, sex, phenotype
├── pipeline_info/
│   ├── params_*.json
│   └── *software*versions*.yml
├── multiqc/multiqc_data/multiqc.parquet
├── alignment/<sample>_sorted_md.metrics.txt               # MarkDuplicates (+ BAM and index for the browser)
├── qc_bam/<sample>_{multiplemetrics,wgsmetrics,hsmetrics,mosdepth.mosdepth}.*
├── call_snv/genome/<family>_snv.vcf.gz                    # joint callset
├── rank_and_filter/<family>_{snv,mt}_ranked_*.vcf.gz      # mt: optional
├── repeat_expansions/<family>_repeat_expansion_stranger.vcf.gz   # optional

└── smncopynumbercaller/out/<family>_smncopynumbercaller.tsv      # optional

docs.title: Validation runs
docs.text:
There is no AWS megatest behind this template, so the repository ships no download script for it. It was built on a real test_full run of nf-core/raredisease 3.1.2 executed on the EMBL cluster: a trio on a reduced GRCh37 reference restricted to one autosome and the mitochondrion, at about 1.4x mean coverage. Every route the template reads is present in it.

That depth is far too low for the numbers to mean anything biological: the relatedness estimate is unreliable, the repeat and SMN calls are mostly No call, and there is no X or Y contig, so the sex check reads Not tested. peddy, GENS, the germline CNV caller and structural variant calling were skipped by the run.

docs.title: Ribosome profiling
docs.text:
Ribosome profiling

riboWaltz periodicity QC, the Salmon sample space of both assays, anota2seq translational regulation, translational efficiency per gene and Ribo-TISH against RiboCode ORF calls, next to the pipeline's own MultiQC report.

nf-co.re GitHub

Experimental Pipeline version 2.0.0 latest

The riboseq template follows an nf-core/riboseq run from paired Ribo-seq and RNA-seq libraries to translated ORFs:

  • Overview: the run in four key figures, live findings and four figures, each linked to the tab that explains it
  • Data & QC: the MultiQC report, riboWaltz periodicity of the footprints, and the Salmon sample space of both assays
  • Translation: translational efficiency per gene, pooled over the run, and anota2seq translational regulation per contrast
  • ORFs: ORF classes per library, and where Ribo-TISH, RiboCode and the annotation agree
Live showcase nf-core/riboseq, nf-core test data Open

The persistent Sample filters (the design group, the library and the assay) sit in the left panel and narrow every tab that reads per-library data.

Two assays in one sample sheet

A riboseq run mixes total mRNA libraries (type: rnaseq) and ribosome footprint libraries (type: riboseq). The MultiQC and Sample space tabs read both; the riboWaltz, Ribo-TISH and RiboCode panels read the footprint libraries only, and anota2seq pairs the two per contrast. The Assay filter splits them on every tab that reads per-library data.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
Point at a finished runFrom the pipeline itself (v1.10.0+) 
depictio ingest /path/to/riboseq_results \
  --template nf-core/riboseq/latest \
  --var METADATA_FILE=/path/to/design.tsv

The hub of the dashboard is the sample sheet the run was started with. It is not part of the published output, so copy it under input/ in the data root, where SAMPLESHEET_FILE is auto-detected, or pass --var SAMPLESHEET_FILE=.... METADATA_FILE is optional: a design table whose first column is the sample id and whose first annotation column becomes the group filter. Without it the design table and the group filter are dropped and every other panel renders from the sample sheet.

depictio config nextflow --install     # once per machine
nextflow run nf-core/riboseq -r 2.0.0 -profile docker --outdir results

No depictio ingest, and no template named: the pipeline ingests its own output directory when it finishes and resolves this template from its own manifest. See Nextflow trigger.

docs.title: Reference
docs.text:
The template reads the sample sheet, the MultiQC report, the Salmon merged gene matrices, the riboWaltz QC tables, the anota2seq results per contrast, the in-frame P-site counts and the Ribo-TISH and RiboCode ORF calls. Every collection past the sample sheet, MultiQC and Salmon is optional, so a run that skipped riboWaltz, the contrasts or an ORF caller still imports. 45 of its 65 tiles carry a use: catalog reference, so a tile says where its panel comes from.

Self-adapting layout

The dashboard adapts to whatever the run actually produced: components bound to pruned or unparsed data collections are hidden, tabs left with no real visualizations are dropped entirely, and the remaining components are re-packed so there are no empty rows.

Pipeline nf-core/riboseq 2.0.0 Template 2.1.0 Updated 1 Nov 2026

docs.title: Template variables
docs.text:
Variables you provide when running the template: DATA_ROOT is the results directory given to depictio ingest, the others are set with --var NAME=value:

Variable Required Description DATA_ROOT ✓ Root directory containing riboseq pipeline output (multiqc/, psites/, quantification/, translational_efficiency/, orf_predictions/) SAMPLESHEET_FILE — Path to the riboseq samplesheet (sample, fastq_1, fastq_2, strandedness, type and the design columns). Auto-detected from {DATA_ROOT}/input/ (CSV or TSV) when omitted. METADATA_FILE — Optional design table (TSV), first column the sample id, then one column per annotation. Adds the group filter and the design table; pruned when absent. METADATA_ID_COL — Design-table sample id column (links join on it). Auto-detected as the first column; defaults to 'sample'. GROUP_COL — Design-table column the group filter and card read. Auto-detected as the first annotation column (treatment in the vendored megatest table). GENOME — UCSC name of the assembly the run aligned to (hg38, hg19, mm10): the axis and gene lane of the genome browser. TRACKS_URI — s3:// or https:// folder holding the run's results (the folder DATA_ROOT mirrors), to read the genome-browser tracks (P-sites, coverage bigWig, BAM) in place instead of uploading them from DATA_ROOT. Without it the tracks collection uploads whichever of those files DATA_ROOT holds.

Auto-detected (set from the run's metadata / params.json; the route flags drive Conditional routes below): GROUP_COL_DISPLAY

docs.title: Data collections
docs.text:
19 data collections — 5 required 14 optional · 14 direct 5 derived.

Origin tells you whether a collection is real pipeline data or a reshape of it: direct = a pipeline output (scanned, or a recipe that reads raw files); derived = a recipe that reshapes one or more direct collections into the layout a visualization needs (no new measurement). Reads shows what produces it: a recipe .py transform, whose name links to its source on GitHub, or a raw file scanned off disk. (A direct collection can still have a recipe — one that merely parses/cleans the raw file; derived means the recipe reshapes another collection.)
